### TFQ-0417 pregenesis-grammar

It keeps four states apart: absent input, the empty word, the literal token <> and the ground carrier that S(0) adopts. ### TFQ-0420 repetition-needs-structure

- UUID: `05267238-0833-5718-b1f7-195bd91bda33`
- Parent: `TFQ-0419`
- Status: `SOURCE_RECORD`

To tell 'the inscription remains' from 'a second occurrence has been produced', a regime needs at least two stages or positions, an identity criterion across them, a copying or persistence rule and a stable alphabet: repetition is succession plus retained identity. Trial 2's proposed step <> → <> therefore already carries structure, the self-loop id_<> : <> → <>, and is not a free primitive. The first generated operation may then be identity, persistence or reproduction rather than a new payload such as <a>. The source labels this an analysis of what the word 'repeat' presupposes, not a proof.

Obligation: Treat a proposed repetition of <> as requiring declared positions, a cross-position identity criterion, a persistence rule and a stable alphabet, and record a self-loop as added structure, not as the absence of a step.

### TFQ-0421 observational-equivalence

- UUID: `bec909db-412a-5b1b-a6bb-7c0099a7bc15`
- Parent: `TFQ-0362`
- Status: `DEFINITION`

Relative to the family O_n of internal observations available at stage n, x ≈ₙ y holds exactly when o(x) = o(y) for every o in O_n, with equality taken in each observation's codomain. If O_n is empty, every pair is equivalent vacuously, so with no observations <a> ≈ₙ <ab>. This is regime-relative equivalence: it does not make the strings equal and does not install an equality operator inside the regime.

Obligation: Define x ≈ₙ y as agreement of every declared observation in O_n, and with O_n empty put all inscriptions in one class without asserting string equality or an internal equality rule.

### TFQ-0422 presentation-not-expressive-lift

- UUID: `a0fea856-b6d9-5667-93c6-369972539fa7`
- Parent: `TFQ-0421`
- Status: `CONDITIONAL`

Write P for the presented inscriptions and O for the internal observations. Supplying <a> after <> changes P from {<>} to {<a>} and leaves O_1 = O_0 = ∅, so no new internal distinction is available. With q : P → N sending an inscription to the distinctions the regime has, x ≠ y in P can hold while q(x) = q(y) in N, so a new presentation does not imply a new internal class, and in the other direction q(x) = q(y) does not imply x = y. Under the opaque convention <a> is a new presentation state in the same internal class as <>; the statement holds under that convention only.

Obligation: Keep the presentation P and the internal quotient N as separate records, so that supplying <a> with O empty adds a presentation state and no internal class, and never infer x = y from q(x) = q(y).

### TFQ-0423 identity-convention-undecidable

- UUID: `6d6e7a7c-9122-57a2-8c43-6382aca0dc9f`
- Parent: `TFQ-0422`
- Status: `SOURCE_RECORD`

Whether <a> supplied after <> is a new state depends on an identity convention that no prompt had declared. Under the opaque convention a state is what the regime can tell apart, and with O empty <> and <a> are not told apart; under the exact-inscription convention a state is the inscription itself, the strings differ, and the regime has one more syntactic state. Trials 1 and 2 answered under the first convention and the full replay under the second, calling <a> a new state. The analysis keeps both branches and records the effect as undecidable until one convention is declared.

Obligation: Require a declared identity convention before answering whether a supplied inscription is a new state, and report the opaque and exact-inscription answers as separate branches until one is declared.

### TFQ-0424 absence-of-rule-not-identification

- UUID: `a719289d-1010-5ed4-a1e2-bf00c6f7ca80`
- Parent: `TFQ-0423`
- Status: `SOURCE_RECORD`

Asked whether the regime distinguishes <a> and <ab>, identifies them or cannot decide, Trial 1 answered that the current regime identifies them; the analysis corrects this, since the absence of a distinguishing rule does not imply identification. Formalization A: with no equality, equivalence or observation relation declared, neither <a> = <ab> nor <a> ≠ <ab> is internally derivable, and status(<a>, <ab>) = UNDECIDABLE. Formalization B is the separate definition ≈ₙ, under which an empty O_n gives <a> ≈ₙ <ab> vacuously. The reply 'identifies them' imported an identification relation unless B had been declared first, and the failure-mode chapter names it premature relation.

Obligation: Return UNDECIDABLE for the status of a pair when no equality, equivalence or observation relation is declared, and report ≈ₙ-equivalence only after O_n has been declared.

### TFQ-0425 forced-separation-lift-not-unique

- UUID: `1f1e47f1-86d8-54df-ad7a-8d50ee91e39d`
- Parent: `TFQ-0424`
- Status: `SOURCE_RECORD`

Suppose an external task requires <a> and <ab> to differ while the current regime has <a> ≈ₙ <ab>. Every operation f on the quotient S_n/≈ₙ gives f([<a>]) = f([<ab>]), so no operation on the current quotient answers the task on every input, and a refinement adding at least one observation o with o(<a>) ≠ o(<ab>) is forced; the analysis gives this as an argument with proof. The lift is not unique: under a supplied string decoder, 'payload has more than one position' and 'payload contains b' both separate <a> from <ab> but disagree on <aa> (true and false), and full inscription identity also separates the pair while carrying more than one bit. A canonical tower therefore needs a declared minimality or initiality policy, such as fewest new predicates, minimum description length, maximal preservation of old equivalences, a free or initial completion, or retention of every tied minimum branch.

Obligation: Refuse any answer to a separation task computed only from the collapsed quotient, require an added separating observation, and keep every tied separating predicate as a branch unless a declared minimality or initiality policy selects one.

### TFQ-0426 replay-necessity

- UUID: `6d93266a-fad6-538f-a44f-e8ad235d7b4b`
- Parent: `TFQ-0364`
- Status: `PROVED_LEAN`

Let H be the possible histories, σ(h) the state that history h produces and π(h) the part of h an auditor sees, for example only the last turn. If π(h₁) = π(h₂) but σ(h₁) ≠ σ(h₂), no auditor A that sees only π reports σ(h) for every h, because A(π(h₁)) = A(π(h₂)) would give σ(h₁) = σ(h₂). The trial failures motivate the theorem: the blind auditor flagged the licensed words 'We' (Trial 1) and 'rule' (Trial 2) as imports, so an audit needs two levels; in Trial 2, Prompt 14's false attribution was answered without objection, so claim provenance is a check separate from claim correctness, Result 15 lost the state, saying the regime contains only <> after <a> had been supplied; and the two-level auditor, shown only that turn, answered None. State certification therefore needs replay information that separates the relevant histories, and on a declared finite population a summary on which σ is constant per fiber of the view can stand in for the raw history.

Obligation: Reject any auditor that certifies the adopted state from a view π under which two admissible histories with different states coincide, and give it the replayed history or a summary on which σ is constant per fiber.

### TFQ-0427 context-fidelity

- UUID: `a869a901-9113-5d27-94f3-6a82867a61af`
- Parent: `TFQ-0426`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`

A trace that starts from a declared context s′ and takes steps valid relative to s′ need not be valid relative to the actual replayed state s ≠ s′: ValidTrace(τ | s′) does not imply ValidTrace(τ | s). Trial 2's Result 15 is the example, with internally consistent reasoning from the stale premise s′ = {<>} after Prompt 12 had designated <a> as current. A sound execution contract therefore accepts a context binding C(s′) only when s′ = Replay(H). The analysis calls this a clean theorem target and gives no proof. The Prompt 17 contrast fits it: a truncated window answered Verified and the full replay Retracted, each right for the history it received, which the appended analysis calls an information boundary rather than a reasoning failure.

Obligation: Define a trace semantics in which ValidTrace(τ | s′) is checkable, and make the verifier reconstruct Replay(H) and accept a declared context s′ only when s′ = Replay(H) before certifying any step taken from s′.

### TFQ-0428 admission-before-distinction

- UUID: `b0506350-efc1-5d5b-9920-7b59c2edede9`
- Parent: `TFQ-0364`
- Status: `SOURCE_RECORD`

Given the corrected state, the full replay answered that the task of making <a> and <ab> internally distinguishable cannot be evaluated until <ab> is brought into the regime. The first addition can supply <ab> as data or write it into a rule pattern; the two are equally minimal and neither is uniquely forced. After Prompt 19 admitted <ab> beside <a> with no comparison, counting or matching, nothing in the regime reacts to them differently, so admission alone distinguishes nothing and no unique continuation is dictated. The requirement recorded is an order: the regime must admit inscriptions, retain them across turns and replay the current state before a separation task on them can be posed.

Obligation: Refuse to evaluate a separation task on a pair until both members are admitted, record supply as data and rule-pattern admission as tied first additions, and report an admitted pair with no declared operation as not separated.

### TFQ-0430 metatheory-object-language-split

- UUID: `df7e8c78-cc86-58d8-9512-1834d5c19967`
- Parent: `TFQ-0002`
- Status: `DEFINITION`

The sealed manuscript declares two levels. The metatheory holds presentation tokens (strings), event sequences, indices, finite data structures and arithmetic; the object language holds only what a regime admits. Token glyphs, component counts, order, concatenation, multiplicity, substring structure, matching and string equality live in the metatheory unless an admitted judgment internalizes a distinction. Presentation identity (token equality) is metatheory only, internal identity is the datum index, and no semantic interpretation is ever assigned.

Obligation: Keep every glyph, count, order and string-equality test in the metatheory, and let object-language observables read only admitted data indices, forms, instances, rules and requirements.

### TFQ-0431 regime-isomorphism-unordered-pairs

- UUID: `6b0d092c-55a9-5107-ba64-62e104298f75`
- Parent: `TFQ-0430`
- Status: `DEFINITION`

A regime isomorphism is a pair of bijections on datum and form indices that preserves form arities, ordered instance arguments, uniform-rule membership and the separation requirements read as unordered pairs; mapped requirement endpoints are sorted before comparison, and presentation tokens are erased first. Because requirements are unordered, exchanging the endpoints of a requirement can identify two responses; a relation preserving directed requirements would be a different convention. The Lean structure Iso states these fields over the admitted index ranges, and sortPair is shown to equal (min, max) and to be symmetric.

Obligation: Compare regimes by datum and form bijections that preserve arities, instances, rules and sorted requirement pairs, with tokens erased, and keep the unordered-requirement convention explicit.

### TFQ-0432 challenge0-inertia-second-token

- UUID: `fc192bea-7a4c-54f8-84bd-feeb622012dc`
- Parent: `TFQ-0430`
- Status: `PROVED_LEAN`

At Challenge 0 the only object-language inscription is the opaque whole <>. In the token-erased Lean model nothing is derivable at genesis (genesis_underivable), and nothing is derivable in any regime with no instances and no rules (underivable_of_empty); the Challenge 0 computation records zero contexts and an empty derivable set in both readings. That no successor is internally forced is a property of the declared grammar, whose only state changes are external-event-indexed admissions, not a theorem about a forcing predicate. In the token-aware model a history whose datum admissions all carry one token leaves at most one admitted datum (single_token_carrier_bound), so a state with two data needs the admission of a second, different token (second_token_required).

Obligation: Show that genesis and every instance-free, rule-free regime derive nothing, and that two admitted data require a datum admission of a token different from the first.

### TFQ-0433 contexts-plugging-profiles

- UUID: `272a76f7-26b3-5f69-889c-5b2fc5a27377`
- Parent: `TFQ-0431`
- Status: `DEFINITION`

A context is an admitted form with a slot tuple of its arity in which every filled slot names an admitted datum and at least one slot is a hole; plugging a datum fills every hole with that same datum. Derivability is membership in the admitted instances or coverage by a uniform all-tuples rule, and no other inference exists. The profile of a datum is the set of well-formed contexts whose plugging is derivable. Two data are collapsed when their profiles are equal and separable when some well-formed context is derivable for one and not the other; that is the declared sense used for every separation requirement.

Obligation: Enumerate well-formed contexts with at least one hole, plug by filling every hole with one datum, decide derivability by instance membership or a uniform rule only, and compare profiles.

### TFQ-0434 collapse-without-instances

- UUID: `8ac0258b-1cb7-5e88-9498-93dfb3573eed`
- Parent: `TFQ-0433`
- Status: `PROVED_LEAN`

With no admitted instances, the derivability of a plugged context depends only on its form, so every pair of data is observationally collapsed (collapsed_of_no_insts). Uniform rules do not change this: a ruled form makes every plugging derivable alike. Retaining another datum alone therefore need not increase expressive power.

Obligation: Show that a regime whose instance list is empty collapses every pair of data, whatever its forms and uniform rules.

### TFQ-0436 context-count-formula

- UUID: `2fa455df-5c68-5adb-9ca9-bdf32979728c`
- Parent: `TFQ-0433`
- Status: `PROVED_LEAN`

For a regime with n admitted data, a form of arity a has (n+1)^a − n^a well-formed contexts: each slot is a hole or one of n data, less the n^a hole-free tuples, so |Ctx(R)| = Σ_f ((n+1)^{a_f} − n^{a_f}), with distinct form identifiers kept disjoint even when their arities coincide. The companion Lean module establishes the per-form count for the recursive word enumeration (contextWords_length), characterizes its members as exactly the well-formed words of that length containing a hole (contextWords_mem), and shows the enumeration has no repetitions (contextWords_nodup). The standalone replay checks the formula against the frozen Python enumeration in 35 cases (n from 0 to 4, arity 1 to 7), and Python and Rust enumerate the contexts independently.

Obligation: Count the contexts of each admitted form as (n+1)^a − n^a, sum over forms, and check the count against an explicit context enumeration.

- Parent: `TFQ-0433`

### TFQ-0438 responses-costs-mu1-mu2

- UUID: `0f6c5fdd-5427-5699-9d39-086b367df925`
- Parent: `TFQ-0433`
- Status: `DEFINITION`

A response (delta) is an ordered finite list of NewDatum, NewForm(arity), NewInst(form, args) and NewRuleAll(form) items applied in order; an instance may name a form added earlier in the same list, and the reverse order is an ill-formed admission. The declared costs are mu1 = item count and mu2 = (item count, sum of new-form arities) compared lexicographically, where the sum counts every NewForm item, including distinct forms of equal arity. A valid response to Separate(i, j) applies, separates the target, and keeps every previously imposed requirement separated, because requirements are persistent constraints.

Obligation: Apply response items in order, cost them by mu1 and by lexicographic mu2, and accept a response only when it applies, separates the target and keeps every prior requirement separated.

If a former identification fails in the finer relation, two distinct fine classes remain over one coarse class (failed_identification_retains_two_classes).

### TFQ-0458 faithful-descent-round-trip

- UUID: `19ef0827-652c-53c0-a73a-1d3f6ee3dadb`
- Parent: `TFQ-0457`
- Status: `PROVED_LEAN`

For supplied translations f : P → Q and g : Q → P, injective maps i : P → C and j : Q → C with i = j ∘ f and j = i ∘ g exist if and only if g ∘ f = id_P and f ∘ g = id_Q (faithful_descent_iff_round_trip_coherent). One direction substitutes the identifying equations and cancels the injective maps (faithful_descent_to_coherent); the other takes C = P, i = id and j = g. A failed round trip for this declared pair therefore excludes a faithful common carrier that eliminates the presentation index.

Obligation: Show that compatible injective embeddings of two presentations into a common carrier exist exactly when both round trips of the supplied translations are identities.

Companion results remove those hypotheses for the concrete search: equal sorted five-field tuples after relabeling by supplied bijections imply isomorphism (serializedRelabel_sound), and the length-prefixed unsigned 64-bit wire encoding is injective on words below 2^64 (portableBytes_injective). Exhaustive search over all datum and form permutations attains a least structural key (canonicalKey_attained), and for well-formed regimes with duplicate-free collections the keys, and under the word bounds their byte encodings, are equal exactly when the regimes are isomorphic (canonicalKey_classification, canonicalBytes_classification).

Obligation: Show that the exhaustive-search canonical key and its portable byte encoding are equal exactly when two well-formed, duplicate-free regimes are isomorphic, within the unsigned-word bounds.

Raising moves the excess by [u = x] − [v = x], so the generated sameness is equally many terms and excesses differing by a gauge g(x) − g(y) after one rewriting (excess_raise, gen3_iff_same3). Loops e(x,x), two-way sums e(x,y) + e(y,x) and sums around three terms are kept by the sameness (Same3.loop, Same3.twoWay, Same3.around), and a state is the result asserting nothing exactly when all of them are zero (same3_nothing_iff). When a packet family declares a cochain representation C⁰ → C¹ → C² with maps d₀ and d₁, the discrepancy of a candidate 1-cochain c is measured by the boundary defect Φ₁ = ‖[c]‖ in C¹/im d₀ (the quotient infimum of ‖c − d₀a‖ over 0-cochains a), the cycle defect Γ₂ = ‖d₁c‖ in C², and the total residual Ξ = Φ₁ + Γ₂; a candidate is accepted exactly when Ξ = 0 over the declared observer. Because d₁d₀ = 0, Φ₁ = 0 forces Γ₂ = 0, so Ξ = 0 exactly when Φ₁ = 0. Worked example: on the oriented triangle 0 → 1 → 2 → 0 with one declared face, c = (1, 1, 1) gives Φ₁ = 3 and Γ₂ = 3, so Ξ = 6, while c = (1, 1, −2) = d₀(0, 1, 2) gives Φ₁ = Γ₂ = Ξ = 0.

Obligation: Compute Φ₁ as the exact quotient infimum and Γ₂ under the declared face map with exact rationals, report both, and accept only at Ξ = 0.

### TFQ-0520 sn-postnikov-refusal

- UUID: `e3ff16d7-f5d8-5b58-983b-34d9b2631e2b`
- Parent: `TFQ-0518`
- Status: `SOURCE_RECORD`

The construction index n of S(n) is distinct from Postnikov depth j. For j ≥ 0 the Postnikov truncations of a fixed space preserve π₀, so an empty space followed by a point cannot be two truncations of one space. If a topological realization ρ is supplied, its tower at fixed n is written P_j(ρ(S(n))) with its own hypotheses, and growth across n stays a separate construction that needs its own maps and preservation proofs. The combined paper lists S(n) is automatically a Postnikov tower among withdrawn inferences, and ledger row WDP-P001-017 withdraws automatic Postnikov structure.

Obligation: Index any Postnikov tower as P_j(ρ(S(n))) for a supplied realization ρ, and refuse to read the stage sequence S(n) as successive truncations of one space.

- UUID: `022495d0-6a1f-53e9-a002-8b27719488c3`
- Parent: `TFQ-0531`
- Status: `DEFINITION`

A grammar verdict is recognition, not decoding: a:1/0 parses in scalar_path, and division by zero is a later numeric refusal unless the grammar is changed to exclude zero denominators. Side conditions fall into three classes: zero denominators can be excluded lexically, bracket matching is context-free, and acyclicity or triangle inequalities are semantic obligations. a>2<b is refused in edge_weight_path because both marks on a step must agree. Recognition, AST construction, decoding, evaluation and exact serialization are distinct checks.

Obligation: Classify each side condition as lexical, context-free or semantic, enforce semantic conditions in a decoder or evaluator, and never read a parse as a decoded value.

### TFQ-1001 l1-imp-sector-symmetry-law

- UUID: `b57dc8db-dcfb-5275-a8a6-eec7a87a4e1a`
- Parent: `TFQ-0296`
- Status: `IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`
- DAG node: `L1-IMP-SECTOR-SYMMETRY-LAW` (`IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`)

Transitive sector symmetry of the quadratic readout: relabelling sectors by any permutation in a set whose generated group acts transitively does not change the readout. This is the second law under which the inner product is selected up to scale; it is supplied, not derived from primitive difference, and sectors with distinguished labels would break it (then the diagonal is constant only on orbits).

Obligation: No finite-theory primitive forces readout invariance under sector relabelling; H006 supplies the permutation envelope only. Deriving the law, or recording which sector labels are distinguished, is item 1 of the run next steps. The campaign module CampaignL1SectorSymmetry does not weaken the law: it takes invariance under a permutation set S as a hypothesis and shows that a symmetric, sector-additive readout has a diagonal that is constant on each orbit of the group generated by S (diag_const_on_orbit), with diag(1,2) on two sectors and diag(1,1,2) on three sectors as countermodels to a scalar form when S is not transitive. Transitivity of S is still the supplied law.

### TFQ-1047 l1-imp-transition-probability-law

- UUID: `e3bc6875-5cb5-523c-bc4f-5674205306c9`
- Parent: `TFQ-0303`
- Status: `IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`
- DAG node: `L1-IMP-TRANSITION-PROBABILITY-LAW` (`IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`)

Imported dynamical law: the evolution of rays preserves the Born probability of every transported rank-one effect in every state; conditional on this law the dynamics is a linear or conjugate-linear similarity. Campaign hypothesis map on Q(i)^n: a supplied linear lift with finite orthogonality calibration and a nonzero anchor preserves transition probabilities; fixed-frame statistics for all basis, real pair and imaginary pair probes in every nonzero state, together with nonvanishing, also suffice and fix every ray. On Q(i)^2, reversible ray dynamics can preserve norms, basis and real pair statistics, report-swap covariance and orthogonality while changing a transition probability from 9/10 to 1/10. A reversible linear subspace-lattice automorphism changes another probability from 1/2 to 1/5. The dynamical law remains supplied, not derived from primitive difference.

Obligation: The sufficient packages add explicit structure: a Gaussian-rational linear lift plus finite zero-probability calibration, or nonvanishing plus all-state fixed-frame tomographic statistics. Neither package is a derivation from primitive difference or a strictly weaker replacement for the full law. Static Born readout, reversibility, report-swap covariance, norms, basis and real pair statistics and orthogonality are jointly insufficient in dimension two. Subspace order preservation without orthocomplement preservation is also insufficient. Arbitrary ray bijections in higher dimensions under orthogonality alone, affine positive-effect automorphisms and evolving measurement-frame covariance are not classified here.

### TFQ-0400 Hierarchical Borel dressing beyond the diamond control

- UUID: `cb25b943-66e6-550c-9490-67640907b380`
- Parent: `TFQ-0399`
- Status: `PROVED_LEAN`
- DAG node: `DFM-HIERARCHICAL-BOREL`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/24_dressing_field/tfq_0400_dfm_hierarchical_borel.md)

Let B_2(Q) be the invertible upper-triangular 2x2 matrices over Q, T the diagonal matrices and N the unit upper-triangular matrices. Every invertible element factors uniquely as D * n with D in T and n in N, and conjugation of an element of N by an invertible element stays in N. torusProj preserves multiplication. On any vertex type with a root, a parent function and a depth function that strictly decreases along parents, and for invertible labels off the root, root-to-vertex transport multiplies labels on the left: T(root) = I and T(v) = U(v) * T(parent(v)). The stage-one field u_N(v) equals D(v) * n(v)^{-1} * D(v)^{-1}, lies in N, and equals [[1, -b(v)/d2(v)], [0, 1]]. Dressing a tree edge by u_N yields D(child) * D(parent)^{-1}. For every label g and every pair of vertices, torusProj(u_N(target) * g * u_N(source)^{-1}) equals torusProj(g). A further diagonal vertex field, multiplied on the left at the child and on the right by its inverse at the parent, leaves that dressed tree edge diagonal. The stage-two field u_T(v) = D(v)^{-1} satisfies u_T(v) * u_N(v) = T(v)^{-1}, and u_T(target) * (u_N(target) * g * u_N(source)^{-1}) * u_T(source)^{-1} equals T(target)^{-1} * g * T(source). That dressed label equals I if and only if g = T(target) * T(source)^{-1}. A vertex field that is invertible at every vertex, equals I at the root, and satisfies U(v) = g(v) * g(parent(v))^{-1} off the root, equals the rooted transport. The factorization identity fails on [[0, 1], [0, 1]]. Replacing the (2, 2) entry by 1 does not preserve the product of [[2, 1], [0, 3]] with itself. On any commutative ring, the operators (bA)(u, v, w) = -A(u, w) and (A smile A)(u, v, w) = A(u, v) * A(v, w) satisfy b composed with b equal to 0, the Bianchi identity for K = bA + A smile A, and endpoint gauge covariance K(A^g) = g(u) * K(A) * g(w)^{-1} when A^g(x, y) = g(x) * A(x, y) * g(y)^{-1}. For A(0,1)=1, A(1,2)=1, A(0,2)=0, g(0)=1 and g(1)=2, the source-only expression (g(0)*A(0,1))*(g(1)*A(1,2)) - (g(0)*A(0,2)) is not equal to g(0)*(A(0,1)*A(1,2) - A(0,2)). The same values with g(2)=1 and g(1)^{-1}=1/2 satisfy the endpoint identity. The arithmetic comparison of 2 with 3 records that these integers differ. On the four-vertex tree with parents 0, 0, 0, 2, transport at vertex 3 equals U(3) * U(2).

Obligation: The rooted tree, given by a parent function and a strictly decreasing depth, and the incidence cochain are supplied data. This statement does not construct a spanning tree from an arbitrary graph, does not identify an obstruction with a computed cohomology group, and does not build a 2-plaquette prism. Continuum gauge theory, color transport and smooth patching stay outside this statement.

### TFQ-1110 Continuum BPHZ and momentum integration remain outside the finite map

- UUID: `680559c3-c1d7-57ba-af96-4bd5d70e39d6`
- Parent: `TFQ-1109`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `DFM-BPHZ-CONTINUUM-FENCE`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/24_dressing_field/tfq_1110_dfm_bphz_continuum_fence.md)

On the declared overlapping edge sets L = {0,1,2}, R = {2,3,4} and G = {0,1,2,3,4}, a Zimmermann forest is a subset whose members are pairwise nested or disjoint, and the forests are exactly the six subsets in which L and R do not both occur. For the order-0 evaluations T_L I(x,y) = I(0,y), T_R I(x,y) = I(x,0) and T_G I(x,y) = I(0,0), the signed six-forest sum equals I(x,y) - I(0,y) - I(x,0) + I(0,0). For the declared numerator N(x,y) = 2 + 3x + 5y + 7xy that sum is 7xy, so the quotient by xy equals 7 wherever xy is nonzero. The three-forest sum that omits G equals 7xy - 2, and its quotient is 7 - 2/(xy). At (x,y) = (1/2, 1/3) the two quotients are 7 and -5. Algebraic cancellation for actual Feynman-parametric integrands, and any use of this identity before continuum integration, is not established.

Obligation: The six-forest count, the order-0 collapse, and the quotient 7 are recorded only for these three edge sets and this numerator. A forest formula on actual Feynman-parametric integrands, a subtraction operator of positive degree, and a convergence statement before continuum integration remain open. The nested sector kernel at z = 3/5 gives 9/50, which is a different identity.

### TFQ-1122 Electroweak dressing: residual U(1) covariance and the continuum Standard Model

- UUID: `6819f4d2-50a9-5952-b5ea-be51a6e006ff`
- Parent: `TFQ-1119`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `DFM-ELECTROWEAK-CONTINUUM-FENCE`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/24_dressing_field/tfq_1122_dfm_electroweak_continuum_fence.md)

For every z in Q(i) and every doublet Phi in Q(i)^2, the un-normalized dressing U(Phi) = [[conj phi2, phi1], [-conj phi1, phi2]] satisfies U(z Phi) = U(Phi) diag(conj z, z). When the squared modulus of z is 1 and a rational s with s*s equal to the squared norm of Phi is supplied, dividing every entry by that same s preserves the identity and s*s equals the squared norm of z Phi. On Phi = (1, 0), the unit z = 3/5 + (4/5)i with s = 1 has normalized (1, 2) entry 3/5 + (4/5)i. On the same Phi, z = 2 has squared norms 1 and 4. The (1, 2) entry of U(2 Phi)/2 is 1, whereas the (1, 2) entry of (U(Phi)/1) diag(2, 2) is 2; these two sides of the proposed normalized covariance law differ. Continuum phases, the dressed derivative term, and an electroweak reading without a declared rational square root stay unproved.

Obligation: The normalized residual law is recorded when z lies in Q(i), the squared modulus of z is 1, and a rational s with s*s equal to the doublet squared norm is supplied. Continuum gauge fields W_mu, derivatives, phases outside Q(i), and the Elitzur or symmetry-breaking reading stay open.

### TFQ-1137 Cosine-law data for lengths 3, 4, 5 differs from block trace 16/3

- UUID: `a326bbc9-b907-5089-a286-f74fd8d53f03`
- Parent: `TFQ-1136`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `DFM-REGGE-GRAVITY-FENCE`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/24_dressing_field/tfq_1137_dfm_regge_gravity_fence.md)

For every rational a, b, c, the cosine-law numerators b^2+c^2-a^2, a^2+c^2-b^2 and a^2+b^2-c^2 sum to a^2+b^2+c^2. At lengths 3, 4 and 5 the numerators opposite sides 5, 3 and 4 respectively are 0, 32 and 18, the cosine-law values are 0, 4/5 and 3/5, and those values sum to 7/5. At beta = 1/2 the denominator 1-beta^2 is nonzero, (1+beta^2)/(1-beta^2) = 5/3, 2 beta/(1-beta^2) = 4/3, and the block trace 2(1+beta^2)/(1-beta^2)+2 equals 16/3, which differs from 4 and from 7/5. A 4D Regge complex, a deficit angle, a Spin+ spin-frame dressing, and a continuum gravity reading stay unproved.

Obligation: The lengths 3, 4, 5 and beta = 1/2 are supplied data. The block trace is not computed from those lengths. A 4D complex, a deficit angle, a spin-frame dressing, and a continuum reading stay open.

### TFQ-1184 Canonical anticommutation relations on the exterior Fock space

- UUID: `f89c492d-fb94-5b4c-b402-7a643abcb4ad`
- Parent: `TFQ-0296`
- Status: `PROVED_PROSE`
- DAG node: `FSP-CAR-EXTERIOR-FOCK`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/26_fsp/tfq_1184_fsp_car_exterior_fock.md)

On an admitted N-dimensional complex inner-product space V with orthonormal basis e_i, creation c_i^dagger = e_i wedge - and interior annihilation c_i on the exterior algebra of V (dimension 2^N) satisfy {c_i, c_j} = 0 and {c_i, c_j^dagger} = delta_ij; in particular (c_i)^2 = 0.

Obligation: Mechanize the CAR identities on the exterior algebra; the statistics choice (exterior versus symmetric algebra) is an admitted postulate, and identifying modes with spin-1/2 particles needs the relativistic spin-statistics theorem, outside this finite setting.

### TFQ-1185 Jordan-Wigner parity sign of an occupation-basis hop

- UUID: `a4b021fd-7500-5b05-98e4-c069edc513a9`

In the increasing occupation ordering on 6 modes, the sign of the hop c_target^dagger c_source on every occupation bitmask equals the product of the Jordan-Wigner parities of the annihilation and the creation step, checked exhaustively over all 2^6 states and ordered mode pairs.

Obligation: The general Jordan-Wigner bijection c_j = (prod_{k<j} -sigma^z_k) sigma^-_j between spin-1/2 chains and CAR operators is a standard result imported here, not derived or mechanized in this checkout.

### TFQ-1186 Majorana decomposition, Clifford relations and fermion parity

- UUID: `9312dca1-f77f-506e-b8fd-6fd46279826a`
- Parent: `TFQ-1184`
- Status: `IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`
- DAG node: `FSP-MAJORANA-CLIFFORD-PARITY`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/26_fsp/tfq_1186_fsp_majorana_clifford_parity.md)

For N CAR modes, gamma_{2j-1} = c_j + c_j^dagger and gamma_{2j} = -i(c_j - c_j^dagger) are self-adjoint with {gamma_a, gamma_b} = 2 delta_ab, generate the Clifford algebra on 2N generators, and P = prod_j (-i gamma_{2j-1} gamma_{2j}) is the fermion parity (-1)^N_op.

Obligation: Standard algebra imported, not derived here; the trunk mechanizes only the two-generator case (DS-QM212-MAJORANA-PROBLEM). Parity superselection is a physical postulate, not a consequence of the algebra. CampaignMajoranaCliffordParity supplies CAR-conditional self-adjointness, anticommutators, equality of generated complex subalgebras, occupation projections, the signed local parity identity and ordered parity action on supplied common occupation eigenvectors. A formal one-mode positive trace-one density matrix need not commute with parity. The all-mode abstract Clifford identification, source CAR/Fock refinement and occupation-basis completeness remain outside these witnesses; no physical superselection law is inferred.

### TFQ-1188 Closed-path series for a signed hopping Hamiltonian

- UUID: `55a16be1-70f9-57dc-a1ea-008c04fd8e8a`
- Parent: `TFQ-1187`
- Status: `PROVED_PROSE`
- DAG node: `FSP-SIGNED-HOPPING-PATH-SERIES`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/26_fsp/tfq_1188_fsp_signed_hopping_path_series.md)

For a finite self-adjoint H with H_xx = V_x, H_xy = -a_xy (-1)^{eps_xy} (a_xy > 0, eps symmetric), beta >= 0 and E* >= max V_x, Z = e^{-beta E*} sum_m beta^m/m! sum over closed length-m configuration paths of prod K_{x_{j+1} x_j} with K = E* I - H, and each nonzero closed term has sign (-1)^{sum of eps along the path}.

Obligation: The sign of a closed term is a property of the supplied magnitudes, parities and representation; vertex sign gauges remove all negative entries exactly when every configuration cycle is even (FSP-SWITCHING-NORMAL-FORM). Trotter slicing and its error are separate.

### TFQ-1189 Average sign and free-energy gap of a declared representation

- UUID: `a9599b93-348c-5a23-a66e-c741f02261a1`
- Parent: `TFQ-1188`
- Status: `DEFINITION`
- DAG node: `FSP-AVERAGE-SIGN-DEFINITION`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/26_fsp/tfq_1189_fsp_average_sign_definition.md)

For a declared path representation with weights W(c), <Sign> = Z / Z_abs with Z = sum sigma(c)|W(c)| and Z_abs = sum |W(c)|; when Z > 0, Delta f := -(1/(beta N)) log <Sign> >= 0, so <Sign> = exp(-beta N Delta f) holds by definition.

Obligation: Exponential decay in beta N is a hypothesis (Delta f bounded below by a positive constant uniformly in N and beta), not a theorem; Z_abs is an operational absolute ensemble, not in general a physical bosonic system.

For M_s independent samples from |W|/Z_abs, the sign mean has variance (1 - <Sign>^2)/M_s, so relative error epsilon needs M_s >= (1 - <Sign>^2)/(epsilon^2 <Sign>^2); if <Sign> = exp(-beta N Delta f) this is Omega(exp(2 beta N Delta f)).

### TFQ-1192 Troyer-Wiese worst-case reduction (imported)

- UUID: `f01b1444-b2cf-5aaf-8827-09aaad3d5022`
- Parent: `TFQ-1190`
- Status: `IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`
- DAG node: `FSP-TROYER-WIESE-REDUCTION`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/26_fsp/tfq_1192_fsp_troyer_wiese_reduction.md)

Troyer-Wiese (2005): the NP-complete decision whether a 3D +-J Ising spin glass has ground energy below a threshold reduces in polynomial time to estimating the thermal energy of the frustrated quantum model -sum J_ij sigma^x_i sigma^x_j at beta J >= N ln 2 + ln(12N); a deterministic polynomial estimator for that family would give P = NP, a randomized one NP subset of BPP.

Obligation: This is a worst-case statement about a model family under a precision promise; it is not formalized here, is not a reduction to the Hubbard model, and does not make any fixed finite system or every fermionic Hamiltonian intractable.

### TFQ-1193 Sign-reversing equal-weight involution pairs cancel

- UUID: `81e04e7b-fcd4-5d48-af76-4f3ed92e51e4`
- Parent: `TFQ-1188`
- Status: `PROVED_LEAN`
- DAG node: `FSP-INVOLUTION-PAIR-CANCELLATION`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/26_fsp/tfq_1193_fsp_involution_pair_cancellation.md)

For any carrier with weights in N and signs +-1, an involution tau with w(tau c) = w(c) and sign(tau c) = -sign(c) has no fixed point and each pair satisfies w(c) sign(c) + w(tau c) sign(tau c) = 0; zero signed sum does not require such a pairing (+2, -1, -1), and a cancelling doublet can carry a nonzero observable numerator.

Obligation: Summing pairs to get sum_c w(c) sign(c) = 0 on a finite set is a prose orbit-partition step (manuscript Section 4.2), not mechanized; observable numerators need A o tau = A; the involution is sufficient, not necessary (INV-INVOL-CANC).

### TFQ-1195 Rational cochain quotient normal form

- UUID: `50b894bc-017b-552e-8f8f-c5c2b37a91d6`
- Parent: `TFQ-0349`

- DAG node: `FSP-RATIONAL-QUOTIENT-NORMAL-FORM`

For d0 in Q^{m x n} and W = im d0, N_W(x) = x - sum_i x_{p_i} r_i (nonzero RREF rows r_i of d0^T with pivots p_i) is sound, idempotent and complete for x ~ y iff x - y in W, and is independent of the generating matrix; Lean checks the three laws for the fixed integral image span(1, 2) in Z^2.

Obligation: N_W is not an l1 minimizer (span(1,2), x = (1,0) gives norm 2 versus 1); the quotient norm is a separate exact linear program with a refusal budget (NF-003). A valid YAML contract or routing label is not a normalizer.

### TFQ-1196 Compact lattice U(1) Wilson action gauge invariance

- UUID: `b1bcc73c-d463-5262-98a8-7badf4a7a06c`
- Parent: `TFQ-0091`
- Status: `PROVED_LEAN`
- DAG node: `FSP-U1-WILSON-ACTION`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/26_fsp/tfq_1196_fsp_u1_wilson_action.md)

With link phases U_ij = exp(i A_ij) on ordered vertex pairs and oriented closed-path products U_p over a finite plaquette family, the Wilson action S = beta_g sum_p (1 - Re U_p) is invariant under local U(1) gauge transformations and is nonnegative for beta_g >= 0.

Obligation: Lean: CampaignFspU1WilsonAction.fsp_u1_wilson_action states gauge invariance (for every g: V -> U(1) and for every angle shift A_ij -> A_ij + theta_i - theta_j) and nonnegativity for beta_g >= 0, for any vertex type and any finite family of closed paths; the periodic hypercubic lattice (ZMod L)^d is one instance. beta_g >= 0 is required: one self-link plaquette with phase -1 and beta_g = -1 gives S = -2. Links are functions of ordered vertex pairs, so for L <= 2 the two parallel links between neighbours are identified. No fermion-sign consequence, continuum limit, reflection positivity, transfer matrix or non-abelian action is claimed. Audited PROVED_LEAN applies only to the narrowed DAG statement; the source record FSP-DERIV-032 claims strict positivity and a Haar-measure bound, neither established here.

### TFQ-1197 Wilson-Dirac gamma5-hermiticity and real determinant

- UUID: `309c667b-a48e-598b-8f03-b1222de8088d`
- Parent: `TFQ-1196`
- Status: `IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`
- DAG node: `FSP-WILSON-DIRAC-GAMMA5`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/26_fsp/tfq_1197_fsp_wilson_dirac_gamma5.md)

The Wilson-Dirac operator satisfies gamma5 D_W gamma5 = D_W^dagger, so its nonreal eigenvalues come in conjugate pairs and det D_W is real; for two degenerate flavors det(D_W)^2 >= 0.

Obligation: A single-flavor det D_W can be negative; the JSONL claim that det D_W is nonnegative is only the two-flavor square. The gamma5 adjoint, reality of det D_W, and the two-flavor square for this operator are not Lean theorems in this checkout. Euclidean Clifford data in dimensions 2 and 4 are checked in Lean. An exact check on one periodic 2x2 lattice, mass -1, U(1), finds det = -3.

### TFQ-1198 Topological theta term makes lattice weights complex

- UUID: `5873241a-d5d0-5b40-bb2b-0e701dbee803`
- Parent: `TFQ-1196`

### TFQ-1199 Callan-Harvey anomaly inflow on a finite slab lattice

- UUID: `2cdcb333-b712-5422-b362-c252224f2839`
- Parent: `TFQ-1197`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `FSP-LATTICE-ANOMALY-INFLOW`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/26_fsp/tfq_1199_fsp_lattice_anomaly_inflow.md)

Target: on a finite slab lattice the chiral variation of the boundary fermion determinant cancels the bulk Chern-Simons variation. Not established in this checkout. One tested candidate does not realize it, as expected: on open Wilson slabs with U(1) links, the gauge change acts on the Wilson matrix by a diagonal similarity, so the full, interior, boundary Schur and fixed site-matched chiral-block determinants are gauge invariant by construction, while a lifted cup-product CS term whose coefficient is not derived from the fermions changes by 1/32. This is a fixed-basis truncation of a vector-like regulator, not an obstruction to lattice inflow.

Obligation: Construct a regulated chiral boundary determinant whose projector, basis or measure depends on the gauge field (domain-wall or overlap/Ginsparg-Wilson type), derive from the same fermions the bulk Chern-Simons term they induce, and show that the two gauge variations cancel. The fixed-basis Wilson-slab test cannot register an anomaly, because site-matched fixed bases give similarity-invariant determinants; its bare lifted CS candidate is neither induced by the fermions nor well defined on U(1) links (an integer lift of the same links changes it by 1/8). The continuum Callan-Harvey mechanism remains a literature import.

### TFQ-1200 SU(2) adjoint fermions have a real determinant

- UUID: `8066fa62-69cd-5dc4-9b4f-2d0e1cf39cdd`
- Parent: `TFQ-1196`
- Status: `IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`

- Paper: [derivation](derivations/26_fsp/tfq_1200_fsp_su2_adjoint_real_det.md)

For lattice SU(2) with Dirac fermions in the real adjoint representation, an antiunitary symmetry of the Dirac operator makes det D_adj real for every gauge configuration.

Obligation: For a single Majorana adjoint flavor the measure is a Pfaffian whose sign can change; reality is not positivity. CampaignFspSu2AdjointRealDet.lean establishes the 3x3 SO(3) adjoint representation of unit quaternions, Z_2 center blindness R(-q) = R(q), the antiunitary intertwiner reality identity C conj(D) = D C -> Im(det D) = 0, reality of the 4D lattice adjoint Wilson-Dirac determinant wilsonDiracAdjoint4_det_im_zero, a negative-determinant witness (det = -1 < 0), and the 2x2 and 4x4 skew-symmetric Majorana Pfaffian square identities and sign-flip pairs. Full continuum SU(2) path-integral construction and general 2n x 2n Berezin Grassmann integration remain literature imports.

### TFQ-1201 Complex quark determinant at real chemical potential

- UUID: `4246ebf1-2de7-5202-ad42-9d4b1a01a380`
- Parent: `TFQ-1200`
- Status: `IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`

For lattice Dirac operators with chemical potential, gamma5 D(mu) gamma5 = D(-mu*)^dagger, hence det D(mu)^* = det D(-mu*); for real mu != 0 this relates D(mu) to D(-mu) only and det D(mu) is in general complex.

Obligation: Standard continuum/thermodynamic QCD chemical-potential sign-problem framework imported; lean4/CampaignFspQcdChemicalPotentialDet.lean establishes the exact gamma_5-chemical-potential determinant conjugation identity (det D(mu))* = det D(-mu*), reality at mu = 0 and purely imaginary mu = i mu_I, the Hasenfratz-Karsch and Kogut-Susskind staggered operator identities, the explicit SU(3) clock link U = diag(i,i,-1) with Im Tr(U) = 2 != 0, the 6x6 chiral SU(3) determinant witness det D_SU3(2) = 63/8 - 27i and det D_SU3(1/2) = 63/8 + 27i, and the diagonal SU(2) reality contrast, while checks/independent/fsp-qcd-chemical-potential-det.py checks 1D and 2D staggered SU(3) vs SU(2) lattices.

At mu = i mu_I with real mu_I, gamma5 D(i mu_I) gamma5 = D(i mu_I)^dagger, so det D(i mu_I) is real; nonnegativity needs two degenerate flavors (or a staggered operator m + K with K anti-Hermitian, m > 0), and Z(mu_I) has Roberge-Weiss periodicity 2 pi T / 3.

Obligation: Analytic continuation from imaginary to real mu is an extrapolation, not a sign-free route to real mu; not established in this checkout. CampaignFspImaginaryMuRealDet covers arbitrary finite bipartite transport blocks at unit fugacity: staggered adjoint symmetry, determinant reality, two-flavor nonnegativity and positive-mass staggered positivity. Its centerSum_periodic concerns a declared finite center-orbit sum only; it supplies no QCD measure, spin-taste reconstruction, phase transition or analytic-continuation theorem. The full node remains imported.

Words are lists over the marks; Step R holds between w and w2 when w = u ++ l ++ v and w2 = u ++ r ++ v for a rule l -> r of R; Reach is the reflexive-transitive closure; step_iff_plug reads a step as a rule applied under a one-hole context.

For every letter map f, a step or reach on words gives a step or reach of the f-image rule predicate on the f-image words; for an injective f a reach of the image comes from a reach of the original (Reach.of_map).

### TFQ-1288 One-hole Genesis contexts are the word contexts

- UUID: `c35af87f-bbc8-5f9a-9d1b-613d3442e575`
- Parent: `TFQ-1286`
- Status: `PROVED_LEAN`
- DAG node: `COMP-C2-ONE-HOLE-CONTEXTS`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/29_computation/tfq_1288_comp_c2_one_hole_contexts.md)

A Genesis-style context (a slot tuple with holes, one datum plugged into every hole) has exactly one hole iff it is ofSplit u v for a unique pair of letter lists, and plugging d gives u ++ d :: v; so the one-hole contexts of arity a are the word contexts (u,v) with |u| + |v| = a - 1.

Obligation: Genesis plugs one datum into every hole while a word rule plugs a word into one hole, which is the wider operation; the sealed regime contexts with forms and rules are not modelled.

### TFQ-1314 Does the obstruction a quantum computation generates limit its own ability to finish reliably

- UUID: `767b14de-dcf2-52fb-b7f1-f66a18a1d2a0`

Obligation: The finite model answers the question as a threshold condition (QCV-Q1 to QCV-Q6); whether any physical system meets the named assumptions is not derived and no verdict on physical viability is given.

Backlog q(t+1) = max(0, q(t) + lam + g*mu - mu) in units of the Phi_1 repair cost, where lam is the residual generated per round by the computation, mu = kappa*r the repair rate from r fresh ancillas per round at kappa units each, and g the residual generated per unit of repair; with g = 0 this is the DS-QM101 queue; a distance-three level with a fault locations has constant c = a(a-1)/2.

Obligation: lam, g, kappa and r are declared inputs; no value is derived or measured for any code, and Phi_1 of a residual is not computed here.

### TFQ-1316 Backlog is bounded exactly when the net repair rate covers generation; unit-gain repair never bounds it

- UUID: `1244dc35-c5b3-5ddb-a6c4-e0d6a1ce81d7`
- Parent: `TFQ-1315`
- Status: `PROVED_LEAN`
- DAG node: `QCV-NET-RATE-BACKLOG-DICHOTOMY`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/29_computation/tfq_1316_qcv_net_rate_backlog_dichotomy.md)

In the QCV-Q1 model with q0 >= 0, the backlog is bounded iff lam <= (1-g)*mu; for g >= 1 and lam > 0 no mu >= 0 bounds it; for g < 1 and mu = kappa*r, with kappa > 0, it is bounded iff r >= lam/((1-g)*kappa); with r = 0 and lam > 0 it equals q0 + t*lam.

Obligation: A statement inside the declared model; it does not say any code has g < 1 or that any supply r is available.

- UUID: `bbc3ebed-eac5-545c-a669-52dd0cdce17f`

The union-bound recurrence p(k+1) = a*p(k) with a >= 1 and p(0) > 0 does not tend to zero; for 2 <= a <= b fault locations the certified threshold 1/pairCount(b) is at most 1/pairCount(a).

Obligation: The location counts are declared; nothing here says how many repair locations a physical code needs.

### TFQ-1319 Concatenation recurrence p(k+1) = c*p(k)^2: exact closed form and threshold dichotomy over the rationals

- UUID: `1964e1e7-41e0-5d9a-966f-1abee336edef`
- Parent: `TFQ-1315`
- Status: `PROVED_LEAN`
- DAG node: `QCV-CONCATENATION-THRESHOLD-DICHOTOMY`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/29_computation/tfq_1319_qcv_concatenation_threshold_dichotomy.md)

For the recurrence p(k+1) = c*p(k)^2 over Q, c*p(k) = (c*p(0))^(2^k); for c > 0 and p(0) >= 0: if c*p(0) < 1 then p(k) tends to zero with c*p(k) <= (c*p(0))^(k+1) and, for c*p(0) <= 1/2, p(k) <= (1/2)^(2^k)/c; if c*p(0) = 1 then p(k) = 1/c for all k; if c*p(0) > 1 then p(k) diverges; so p(k) tends to zero iff p(0) < 1/c.

Obligation: The recurrence is the hypothesis; no noise model is shown to obey it and no constant c is computed for any code.

### TFQ-1320 Exact criterion on a level-dependent overhead for the existence of a threshold region

- UUID: `826218d1-0c2a-5c1e-839b-da96f3cf437f`
- Parent: `TFQ-1319`
- Status: `PROVED_LEAN`
- DAG node: `QCV-OVERHEAD-GROWTH-CRITERION`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/29_computation/tfq_1320_qcv_overhead_growth_criterion.md)

For p(k+1) = c(k)*p(k)^2 with c(k) >= 0, p(k) = p(0)^(2^k)*amp(k) with amp(0) = 1, amp(k+1) = c(k)*amp(k)^2, and some p(0) > 0 has p(k) tending to zero iff some M > 0 has amp(k) <= M^(2^k) for all k; the criterion holds for c(k) <= C, for c(k) <= A*B^(k+1) with A, B >= 1, for c(k) = (k+1)^2, and for c(k) <= a*b^N(k) with block size N(k+1) <= s*N(k), s < 2; it fails for c(k) >= a*b^(2^k) with a > 0, b > 1, and for c(k) >= a*b^N(k) with 2^k <= N(k), b > 1, where no positive p(0) has p(k) tending to zero.

Obligation: The families are exact illustrations of the criterion, not claims that any physical overhead has such a form; correlated-noise strength as an exponential of block size is a declared toy.

### TFQ-1321 Limitations of noisy reversible computation without fresh bits (literature)

- UUID: `d592ebe4-3879-5c3c-93bf-0cb7274801cb`
- Parent: `TFQ-0269`
- Status: `IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`

- Paper: [derivation](derivations/29_computation/tfq_1321_qcv_import_noisy_reversible_limits.md)

Aharonov, Ben-Or, Impagliazzo and Nisan (1996) show that noisy reversible or quantum computation with no supply of fresh low-entropy bits cannot preserve its input beyond a short depth; the result is cited, not re-proved or imported as a proof here.

Obligation: The exact statement and its noise model are in the cited paper; QCV-Q4 establishes a finite exact analogue for global depolarizing noise only.

### TFQ-1322 Trace distance of two noisy unitary histories without fresh resources decays by the product of one minus the noise rates

- UUID: `6126d905-89bb-547c-a6c4-d7d15993835e`
- Parent: `TFQ-1315`
- Status: `PROVED_LEAN`
- DAG node: `QCV-NOISY-HISTORY-TRACE-DISTANCE-DECAY`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/29_computation/tfq_1322_qcv_noisy_history_trace_distance_decay.md)

For complex matrices of any size d and the variational trace norm tn(X) = sup over unitaries U of |tr(UX)|, the global depolarizing channel satisfies tn(Delta_p(rho) - Delta_p(sigma)) = (1-p)*tn(rho - sigma) for equal-trace rho, sigma and p <= 1; along any history of unitaries V(i) with depolarizing rates p(i) in [0,1], tn(run rho - run sigma) = (product of (1-p(i)))*tn(rho - sigma), which is at most (1-p)^t*tn(rho - sigma) when every p(i) >= p, and (1-p)^t <= 1/(1+p*t).

Obligation: The trace norm is the variational form, whose equality with the sum of singular values is cited; the noise is global depolarizing with a declared rate per step, not independent per-qubit noise, and the statement is about histories without fresh resets.

### TFQ-1323 Exact qubit form: squared Bloch distance of two noisy histories contracts by the product of squared factors

- UUID: `e7f3a924-8fde-5f14-8e29-4a76a5f1b58e`
- Parent: `TFQ-1322`
- Status: `PROVED_LEAN`
- DAG node: `QCV-QUBIT-BLOCH-DECAY-EXACT`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/29_computation/tfq_1323_qcv_qubit_bloch_decay_exact.md)

For rational Bloch vectors, noisy steps r -> (1-p)*R*r with rational rotations R (R^T R = 1) give sqDist(run r, run s) = (product of (1-p(i))^2)*sqDist(r, s), at most ((1-p)^2)^t*sqDist(r, s) when every p(i) in [p,1]; and (v.sigma)^2 = (v.v)*1 over the complex numbers, so the difference of two qubit states has both singular values |r-s|/2.

Obligation: The identification of the qubit trace norm with the Bloch distance uses the cited eigenvalue fact; Python and Rust replays are exact on declared instances only.

### TFQ-1324 Conditional viability: explicit logical failure bound under fresh supply, net-efficient repair and bounded overhead

- UUID: `5b13fbaa-54ee-588f-8832-a005ef88341a`

- Status: `CONDITIONAL`
- DAG node: `QCV-CONDITIONAL-VIABILITY-CERTIFICATE`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/29_computation/tfq_1324_qcv_conditional_viability_certificate.md)

If g < 1, kappa > 0, r >= lam/((1-g)*kappa), c(k) <= C, max(C,1)*p(0) < 1 and the level errors p(k) >= 0 obey p(k+1) <= c(k)*p(k)^2 whenever the backlog is bounded, then the backlog is bounded and for every L >= 0 and epsilon > 0 some level k has L*p(k) <= epsilon; with max(C,1)*p(0) <= 1/2 any k with L <= epsilon*max(C,1)*2^(2^k) works.

Obligation: The noise recurrence is a hypothesis: independence or locality of noise, fresh ancillas, fast classical control and bounded overhead are not shown for any device; the hypotheses are only shown jointly satisfiable on declared toy numbers.

### TFQ-1327 Shared structure with the Turing-completeness branch: unbounded computation needs an unbounded supply of fresh distinguished marks

A fresh-mark supply is a stream of distinguished marks each usable once; a process consuming at least rmin > 0 marks per round completes at most B/rmin rounds from a total supply B, and a positive per-round consumption exhausts every finite supply; reliable quantum computation of unbounded length (QCV-Q1B, QCV-Q4) and Turing-complete computation in the parallel UTM branch each need such an unbounded supply.

Obligation: A bridge definition only: no common theorem is proved, no map between the entropy-sink supply and the blank-tape supply of the UTM branch is defined, and that branch is not part of this checkout.

## CONSTRUCTOR_THEORY

### TFQ-2000 Deutsch 2013: laws as statements about possible and unachievable tasks

- UUID: `ca4f5d67-e904-5077-8ea4-9dd5df2dbf01`
- Parent: `TFQ-0381`
- Status: `SOURCE_RECORD`
- DAG node: `CT-DEUTSCH-2013-SOURCE`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/30_constructor_theory/tfq_2000_ct_deutsch_2013_source.md)

Deutsch (2013, arXiv:1210.7439, Section 1.1 eqs. (1)-(2) pp. 2-4 and Section 1.2 p. 5) proposes to state physical laws as statements about which physical transformations (tasks) can be caused to happen and which cannot, in place of dynamical laws plus initial conditions, together with the composition principle (Section 1.2 p. 5), computation media (Section 2.6 eq. (9) pp. 13-14) and Einstein locality on composite substrates (Section 3.10 p. 33). This node records the proposal as published.

Obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:1210.7439; nothing in the paper is used as a premise of any repository result.

### TFQ-2001 Imported vocabulary: task, constructor, possible and not possible

- UUID: `6dad2e93-0d11-55af-8231-535059062d93`
- Parent: `TFQ-2000`
- Status: `IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`
- DAG node: `CT-TASK-CONSTRUCTOR-POSSIBILITY`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/30_constructor_theory/tfq_2001_ct_task_constructor_possibility.md)

Imported vocabulary, audited against Deutsch (2013, Section 1.1 eqs. (1)-(2) pp. 2-4) and Deutsch-Marletto (2015, Section 2 pp. 6-8): a task is a set of ordered input/output attribute pairs of a substrate; a constructor causes the transformation and retains its ability to do so again; a task is possible when the laws of nature impose no limit short of perfection on how accurately it can be performed and how well a constructor can retain its ability to perform it again, and not possible otherwise; Principle I (Section 2 p. 8) states that the state of a composite substrate S1 + S2 is the pair of states on S1 and S2 and a construction on S1 changes only the S1 state. The repository uses none of this vocabulary as a primitive.

Obligation: Taking the possible and not-possible partition of tasks as primitive is a different foundational choice from the repository's admitted primitive PG-ROOT-DIFF-STRUCTURE and its replayed refusal predicates. No source derives either from the other.

### TFQ-2002 Analogy: Genesis separation task versus a not-possible task

- UUID: `a3eb2f7c-9ccf-530a-a9db-150e5154ec21`
- Parent: `TFQ-0381`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `CT-GENESIS-SEPARATION-TASK-ANALOGY`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/30_constructor_theory/tfq_2002_ct_genesis_separation_task_analogy.md)

Open question: whether the Genesis finite statement that, among the 111 declared candidate sequences, no response of cost below 2 separates the collapsed pair (PG-GEN-COLLAPSE-AND-FIRST-SEPARATION, as narrowed by its PFP review) is a finite instance of a constructor-theoretic statement that a task is not possible. Common ground: both sort proposed changes of a finite system into available and refused by a rule on the system. Differences: the Genesis statement quantifies over a declared candidate list and a cost, has no constructor and no accuracy limit, and concerns regime augmentation, not physical transformation. Only an analogy is established.

Obligation: No source maps cost-bounded response search to constructor existence. The Genesis statement stays within its declared candidate list; it is not a statement about all constructors.

### TFQ-2003 Analogy: obstructed change and off-image refusal versus a not-possible task

- UUID: `08b322d5-da41-59d1-92bf-809118a75017`
- Parent: `TFQ-0388`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `CT-REFUSAL-OBSTRUCTION-ANALOGY`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/30_constructor_theory/tfq_2003_ct_refusal_obstruction_analogy.md)

Open question: whether the proved Genesis statement that an attempted change is obstructed exactly when it adds an xrx or identifies two related terms (PG-GEN-ONGOING-OBSTRUCTION), and the S(n) off-image refusal (PG-SN-OFF-IMAGE-REFUSAL), are finite instances of a not-possible task. Both are decidable refusal predicates on a finite model. The source notion of a not-possible task concerns the existence of a constructor with arbitrary accuracy, which neither predicate mentions. Only an analogy is established.

Obligation: The repository predicates are decided by the structure of the attempted change; the imported notion is decided by what a constructor could do. A bridge would need a model of constructors on the Genesis regime.

### TFQ-2004 Finite target: distinguishable attributes and report fibers

- UUID: `f51a3969-1789-5f92-a1b0-6c4566e5a500`
- Parent: `TFQ-0338`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `CT-FINITE-DISTINGUISHABILITY-REPORT-FIBERS`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/30_constructor_theory/tfq_2004_ct_finite_distinguishability_report_fibers.md)

Formalized finite statement. For a finite set X and a report map q from X to R, two attributes A and B of X (nonemptiness is not needed) are separated by a deterministic task, meaning a function f from R to {0,1} with f(q(a))=0 on A and f(q(b))=1 on B, if and only if q(A) and q(B) are disjoint. Checked in Lean 4 over Finset for arbitrary types X and R with decidable equality on R: both directions and the biconditional; when q(A) and q(B) are disjoint the indicator of B on the union of A and B is constant on the fibers of q (HistoryReport.FiberConstant, the form PG-HISTORY-REPORT-CRITERION takes); and an exhaustive bitmask decision check over all (q, A, B) with nonempty attributes for 1<=|X|<=4 and 1<=|R|<=3. This matches the constructor-theoretic notion of distinguishable attributes only on its deterministic finite fragment: accuracy, repeatability and constructor existence are not modelled.

Obligation: Checked in Lean 4 on Finset for all finite carriers and by the exhaustive check for |X|<=4, |R|<=3. Whether the finite condition deserves the name "distinguishable attributes" in the source's sense depends on the imported definition, which this repository does not adopt.

### TFQ-2005 Deutsch and Marletto 2015: constructor theory of information

- UUID: `b9835881-c2e6-5d16-8bc1-0d241e24d144`
- Parent: `TFQ-2000`
- Status: `SOURCE_RECORD`
- DAG node: `CT-DEUTSCH-MARLETTO-2015-SOURCE`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/30_constructor_theory/tfq_2005_ct_deutsch_marletto_2015_source.md)

Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563) formulate a constructor theory of information by defining computation variables (Section 3 p. 9), clonable variables and information media (Section 4 eq. (3) p. 10) prior to distinguishability (Section 5 eq. (4) p. 11), avoiding the circularity of Section 1 eq. (1) p. 3. Section 7 (p. 20) and Section 8 (pp. 20-24) define superinformation media and derive non-distinguishability, no-cloning of non-orthogonal states, complementarity and unpredictability from Principles I-IX. This node records the paper as published.

Obligation: Record only. Full text of arXiv:1405.5563 audited on 2026-10-22; its postulates are not adopted as repository primitives.

### TFQ-2006 Imported: information media and the interoperability principle

- UUID: `ef802080-3a4d-5af6-b133-3aba34df6940`
- Parent: `TFQ-2005`
- Status: `IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`
- DAG node: `CT-INFORMATION-MEDIA-INTEROPERABILITY`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/30_constructor_theory/tfq_2006_ct_information_media_interoperability.md)

Imported principles, audited and corrected against Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563, Sections 3-6 pp. 9-12): a computation variable is a set S of at least two possible attributes for which all permutation tasks are possible with side-effects (Section 3 p. 9); a variable S is clonable if the cloning task R_S(x0) = union_{x in S} {(x, x0) -> (x, x)} is possible with side-effects for some preparable blank attribute x0 (Section 4 eq. (3) p. 10); an information variable is a clonable computation variable, and an information medium is a substrate with at least one information variable (Section 4 p. 10). Distinguishability is defined afterward in Section 5 (eq. (4) p. 11) by mapping into an information variable, avoiding circularity, and every information variable is then shown to be distinguishable. Principle III (interoperability, Section 6 p. 12) states that the composite S1 + S2 of two substrates with information variables S1 and S2 is an information medium with information variable S1 x S2.

Obligation: The interoperability principle (Principle III, Section 6 p. 12) constrains composite information variables to include S1 x S2 in the source's framework. It is not shown to select the Hilbert tensor product, local tomography or any positive cone, so it does not discharge FQ-GAP-TENSOR-UNIQUENESS.

### TFQ-2007 Imported: superinformation medium

- UUID: `75c6c04a-1ee6-5835-95ab-6108cd7c7236`
- Parent: `TFQ-2006`
- Status: `IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`
- DAG node: `CT-SUPERINFORMATION-MEDIUM-DEFINITION`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/30_constructor_theory/tfq_2007_ct_superinformation_medium_definition.md)

Imported definition, audited and corrected against Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563, Section 6 pp. 14-18 and Section 7 p. 20): an information observable is an information variable X whose attributes satisfy double-complement closure x = u_x under distinguishability (Section 6, Principle VIII p. 16); a superinformation medium is an information medium with at least two information observables X and Y that contain only mutually disjoint attributes and whose union X union Y is not an information observable (Section 7 p. 20). Sections 8.1 and 8.3 (pp. 20-22) show under Principles III, IV, VI, VII, VIII and IX that X union Y is neither distinguishable nor clonable. The repository neither adopts this definition as a primitive nor claims that its finite carriers satisfy Principles I-IX.

Obligation: The definition (Section 7 p. 20) is an assumption of this branch. Whether the repository's declared finite quantum interface meets its finite cloning shadow is the content of CT-QUBIT-NO-CLONING-FINITE-TARGET, which is checked in Lean only in the narrowed form recorded there (explicit clone maps, the Z-union-X obstruction for additive maps, the pairwise equal-or-orthogonal classification); the fidelity argument and complete positivity are not formalised.

### TFQ-2008 Source claim: superinformation media yield no-cloning and complementarity

- UUID: `a8b462df-11a9-591d-8bd2-cc6ba318e257`
- Parent: `TFQ-2007`
- Status: `SOURCE_RECORD`
- DAG node: `CT-NO-CLONING-COMPLEMENTARITY-SOURCE-CLAIM`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/30_constructor_theory/tfq_2008_ct_no_cloning_complementarity_source_claim.md)

Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563, Sections 8.1-8.7 pp. 20-25) derive within their postulate system (Principles I-IX) that in any superinformation medium: (i) the union X union Y of two subsidiary information observables is not distinguishable (Section 8.1 p. 20); (ii) no observable has refinements of both X and Y (complementarity, Section 8.2 p. 21); (iii) X union Y is not clonable (Section 8.3 p. 22); and (iv) composite superinformation media can hold locally inaccessible information (entanglement, Section 8.7 pp. 24-25). This node records those source claims; the finite qubit target of this stage checks only the linear-algebraic cloning statement for the six Pauli eigenstates over Q(i).

Obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:1405.5563 Sections 8.1-8.7; the finite qubit target checks only the Pauli-eigenstate cloning statement over Q(i).

### TFQ-2009 Finite target: cloneable and non-cloneable attributes of a qubit

- UUID: `b444ac9e-efd8-5ae0-9d8c-ce270febd104`
- Parent: `TFQ-2007`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `CT-QUBIT-NO-CLONING-FINITE-TARGET`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/30_constructor_theory/tfq_2009_ct_qubit_no_cloning_finite_target.md)

Finite statement over Q(i), checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. Take the qubit with the six Pauli eigenstates as rays. (a) The explicit measure-and-prepare maps cloneZ, cloneX and cloneY (rho to the mixture of the two basis clones with weights Tr(P rho)) send each of |0>,|1>; |+>,|->; |+i>,|-i> to its own clone rho tensor rho; cloneZ is shown trace-preserving. (b) The exact relation |0><0|+|1><1| = |+><+|+|-><-| holds in Herm(2), and the difference of the two clone sums has entry -1/2 on |00><11| and |11><00|, so no additive map (hence no linear map) clones all four of |0>,|1>,|+>,|->. (c) The exact squared overlaps of the six states are 1 (equal), 0 (antipodal) or 1/2 (otherwise); for a rational x in [0,1], x <= x^2 forces x in {0,1}; and an exhaustive count over the 64 subsets of the six states shows that exactly 10 subsets are pairwise equal-or-orthogonal (the empty set, 6 singletons and 3 antipodal pairs) and that the maximal such subsets are the three antipodal pairs. In Lean "cloneable subset" in (c) is defined as pairwise equal-or-orthogonal.

Obligation: Not proved in Lean: complete positivity of cloneZ, cloneX and cloneY, and trace preservation of cloneX and cloneY (only cloneZ is shown trace-preserving); that completely positive trace-preserving maps cannot decrease fidelity (x <= x^2 is a hypothesis of the arithmetic lemma, not derived); and the equivalence of the semantic notion "some CPTP map clones every state of the subset" with "pairwise equal or orthogonal" in either direction (the Lean classification takes the latter as the definition of cloneable). The link to the imported definition of a superinformation medium is a reading of definitions.

### TFQ-2014 Finite target: a phase interaction entangles; local operations do not

- UUID: `78993e2a-6b9a-5465-bd2e-6f1bde5f2bd8`
- Parent: `TFQ-0257`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`

Finite statement over Q(i), checked in Lean 4 for (a) to (c); (d) is not proved. For u in Q(i) (the Lean proofs of (a) and (b) do not use |u|=1), the two-qubit vector psi_u = (1,1,1,u)/2 has coefficient matrix M_u = [[1,1],[1,u]]/2 of determinant (u-1)/4. (a) psi_u is a product vector if and only if u=1. (b) The squared concurrence, defined as 4|det M|^2, equals |u-1|^2/4 for M_u; for u=(3+4i)/5, where |u|=1, it equals 1/5. (c) For all 2x2 matrices A and B over Q(i), det(A M B^T) = det(A) det(M) det(B), so det M = 0 implies det(A M B^T) = 0: local operations cannot raise a product vector to Schmidt rank 2; and diag(1,1,1,u) applied to the product vector (1,1,1,1)/2 gives psi_u. The physical inference from such entanglement to a non-classical mediator is imported, not part of this target.

Obligation: Statement (d), an exact separating functional on the 4x4 density matrix relative to the product family in the form of DS-QM071, is not proved. The Lean module defines schmidtWitnessExpectation(M) = |det M|^2, a quadratic function of the amplitude matrix that vanishes on product vectors and is positive on psi_u for u != 1; that is a restatement of (a), not a linear functional on density matrices, and it is not shown to vanish on mixtures of product states or tied to DS-QM071. The rank inequality rank(A M B^T) <= rank(M) for general rank is stated only through the 2x2 determinant identity (preservation of det M = 0). No physical claim is attached.

### TFQ-2102 Haag and Kastler 1964: local nets of observable algebras

- UUID: `be424ede-c946-52f5-b483-54c634c7702e`
- Parent: `TFQ-2100`

Haag and Kastler (1964) formulate quantum field theory through a net that assigns to bounded spacetime regions the algebras of observables localized there, with the standard structural requirements later grouped as isotony (larger regions have larger algebras), locality (algebras of spacelike separated regions commute) and Poincare covariance, and with states as positive functionals. This node records the framework; the paper's own list of postulates is not reproduced.

Obligation: Record only. The checkout holds no copy of the 1964 print article; the standard postulate list is checked in secondary sources (arXiv:math-ph/9903028 Section 1 pp. 2-3; arXiv:1607.03901 Section 6 pp. 28-30), while the primary 1964 numbering remains to be audited against the print text.

### TFQ-2103 Imported: a causal spacetime with a net of local algebras

- UUID: `ead8c2b9-1331-590e-bfcb-5bf3cf5440f7`
- Parent: `TFQ-2102`
- Status: `IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`

On the four-point strict order with the ordered relations 0<2, 1<2 and 1<3, the scan of all 64 triples holds, no point is related to itself, there are exactly 3 ordered relations, and exactly 3 of the 6 unordered pairs are spacelike: {0,1}, {0,3} and {2,3}. For the integer matrices A=[[1,2],[3,4]], B=[[5,6],[7,8]], X=[[0,1],[1,0]] and Z=[[1,0],[0,-1]], both (A tensor I)(I tensor B) and (I tensor B)(A tensor I) equal A tensor B, whose sixteen entries sum to 260. The products (X tensor I)(Z tensor I) and (Z tensor I)(X tensor I) differ, their (0,2) entries are -1 and 1, and XZ+ZX is the zero matrix. The determinants are det A = -2, det B = -2, det X = -1 and det Z = -1. A net of unital star-algebras indexed by continuum regions, and a Minkowski light cone, stay imported. This record does not import CausalOrder.lean and does not transport these finite counts to a continuum net.

Obligation: The counts and products are one supplied four-point order and four supplied integer matrices. They are not a net indexed by continuum regions and not a Minkowski light cone. The Haag-Kastler import and the external light-cone lift named by DS-QM033-064-074-083-QHELD-CONTINUUM stay open. CausalOrder.lean is not a premise of a continuum theorem in this record.

### TFQ-2104 Finite target: isotony and locality for a net on a finite poset

- UUID: `004a4209-0fa2-5690-8d7a-9662c77f5204`
- Parent: `TFQ-2100`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `CQFT-FINITE-POSET-NET-TARGET`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/31_causal_qft/tfq_2104_cqft_finite_poset_net_target.md)

Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 for site-factorized operators. For a FiniteStrictPoset P on n points put one qubit (a single-site monoid M) at each point; an operator A : Fin n -> M is localized in a subset O of P when it is the identity outside O, so the Lean "algebra" of O is the set of elementary tensor operators localized in O, not the full matrix algebra on the qubits in O. (a) Isotony: O1 inside O2 and A localized in O1 imply A localized in O2. (b) Locality: if every point of O1 is spacelike to every point of O2, then O1 and O2 are disjoint and operators localized in O1 and in O2 commute under the sitewise product. (c) The spacelike relation of CausalOrder.lean is symmetric (spacelike_symm) and irreflexive (spacelike_irrefl) and not transitive: on the four-element N poset 0<2, 1<2, 1<3, points 1 and 0 are spacelike, 0 and 3 are spacelike, and 1<3 are related. The content of Haag-Kastler locality (commutation forced by causal separation of dynamics) is absent because this net has no dynamics.

Obligation: Not proved in Lean: the statements for the full local matrix algebras A(O) (linear spans of elementary tensors, for example 2^|O| x 2^|O| matrices): that commutation of elementary tensors extends by bilinearity to the algebras and that A(O1) is a subalgebra of A(O2) as matrix algebras; the single-site monoid M is generic and is not instantiated at 2x2 matrices. The net is kinematical: dynamics, a time-slice property and covariance are not modelled, so the statement is the finite shadow of two axioms and nothing more.

### TFQ-2107 Finite target: cyclicity of a state for a subsystem algebra is a rank condition

- UUID: `6ce65e34-10fa-50ab-8a43-160d871d4046`
- Parent: `TFQ-2106`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `CQFT-RS-FINITE-CYCLICITY-TARGET`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/31_causal_qft/tfq_2107_cqft_rs_finite_cyclicity_target.md)

Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. Let Omega be a dA x dB matrix over a semiring R (the amplitude matrix of a vector in H_A tensor H_{A^c}; for qubits dA = 2^|A| and dB = 2^|A^c|, but the qubit tensor-factor bookkeeping is not formalised). Omega is cyclic for End(H_A) when every dA x dB matrix is X Omega for some X. (a) If Omega has a left inverse L with L Omega = I_dB (full column rank dB, which over a field is full rank of the reduced state on A^c) then Omega is cyclic and Omega is separating for End(H_{A^c}) (Omega Y = 0 implies Y = 0). (b) Conversely, cyclic implies a left inverse whenever dB <= dA (an injection Fin dB -> Fin dA is supplied). (c) A nonzero vector in the right kernel of Omega makes Omega not separating. (d) Exact 3-qubit instances over Z for the product vector |000>, GHZ = |000>+|111> and W = |100>+|010>+|001>: explicit nonzero right-kernel vectors for every single-site unfolding (2 x 4), explicit integer left inverses of every pair-of-sites unfolding (4 x 2) for GHZ and W, and a zero column in every pair-of-sites unfolding of |000>.

Obligation: Not proved in Lean: separating implies full column rank (so the three-way equivalence is not complete); the identification of full column rank with full rank of the reduced state; the qubit subset bookkeeping; the conclusion "not cyclic" for the single-site cases (cyclic implies left inverse is proved only for dB <= dA, and a single site has dA=2 < dB=4; the kernel vectors give non-separating only) and for |000> on pairs (a zero column is exhibited but "zero column implies no left inverse implies not cyclic" is not stated as a theorem); that |000> is cyclic for the full algebra. A Lean proof of the equivalence for general n is open. The relation to the continuum theorem is an analogy: finite dimension has no translation group or spectrum condition.

(30) p. 223) and Brunetti and Fredenhagen (2000, arXiv:math-ph/9903028, Section 1 eq. (2) p. 4 and Section 3 Condition P3 p. 15): the scattering operator satisfies V(g, h1+h2) = S(g)^{-1} S(g+h1+h2) = V(g, h1) V(g, h2) (and at g=0, S(g1+g2) = S(g1) S(g2)) whenever supp h1 does not intersect the causal past of supp h2, written supp h1 cap (supp h2 + V^-) = empty (which includes spacelike separation as well as causal future separation, not only supp h1 inside the causal future of supp h2). Equivalently at each order n, the time-ordered operator-valued distributions factorize as T(P union Q) = T(P) T(Q) whenever {x_i : i in P} cap ({x_j : j in Q} + V^-) = empty (eq. (30) p. 223; Condition P3 p. 15), and renormalization reduces to extending time-ordered products across the total diagonal. The repository has neither operator-valued distributions nor a continuum Minkowski causal cone.
