### TFQ-2111 Bombelli, Lee, Meyer and Sorkin 1987: space-time as a causal set

- UUID: `56cdd3b5-07b1-5050-97d3-5738a97ceda9`
- Parent: `TFQ-2100`
- Status: `SOURCE_RECORD`
- DAG node: `CQFT-BLMS-1987-SOURCE`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/31_causal_qft/tfq_2111_cqft_blms_1987_source.md)

Bombelli, Lee, Meyer and Sorkin (1987) propose that spacetime at the smallest scales is a discrete structure, a causal set: a locally finite set with a partial order encoding past and future. They examine how a Lorentzian manifold can approximate such a set, note that effective dimensionality can vary with length scale, and sketch a quantum dynamics. Sorkin's Valdivia notes (2003) are a later survey. This node records the proposal.

Obligation: Record only. Sorkin (2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0309009 Section 3 p. 6) and Reid (2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0207103 Section II p. 2) were audited in full; the 1987 PRL print article is not held in the checkout.

### TFQ-2112 A finite causal set is a FiniteStrictPoset

- UUID: `861fbbf4-3a61-5b38-8b52-b555e765df38`
- Parent: `TFQ-2111`
- Status: `DEFINITION`
- DAG node: `CQFT-FINITE-CAUSET-IDENTIFICATION`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/31_causal_qft/tfq_2112_cqft_finite_causet_identification.md)

Reading of definitions. A causal set in the sense of the source is a locally finite partially ordered set; in the strict-order form its relation is irreflexive and transitive, and local finiteness is automatic on a finite set. This is the structure FiniteStrictPoset n of lean4/CausalOrder.lean. The Python class CausalSet in code/python/src/general_relativity/causal_set.py builds a poset from relations, takes the transitive closure and refuses cycles. The identification involves no sprinkling, no embedding in a Lorentzian manifold and no dynamics.

Obligation: Definitional only. Nothing about manifold-likeness, dimension or the continuum limit is asserted.

### TFQ-2113 Finite target: ordering fraction, Myrheim-Meyer dimension and Hasse diagrams as exact rationals

- UUID: `aa6ab549-4ad3-59bb-bd9f-c82bfc9619b6`
- Parent: `TFQ-2112`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `CQFT-MYRHEIM-MEYER-ORDERING-FRACTION-TARGET`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/31_causal_qft/tfq_2113_cqft_myrheim_meyer_ordering_fraction_target.md)

Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. The ordering fraction of a finite causal set is the exact rational r = 2R/(n(n-1)), with R the number of strictly related pairs (CausalSet.ordering_fraction); Lean computes r(C1)=2/3 and r(C2)=5/6 from the relation tables of CausalOrder.lean. In Sorkin (2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0309009 Section 7 p. 16), the expected ordering fraction of a Poisson sprinkling into a d-dimensional Minkowski causal interval normalized by binom(N,2) is f(d) = (3/2) Gamma(d+1) Gamma(d/2 + 1) / Gamma(3d/2 + 1) = Gamma(d+1) Gamma(d/2) / (2 Gamma(3d/2)) (in Reid 2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0207103 Section III eq. (5) p. 5, normalizing by <N>^2 instead of binom(N,2) gives f(d)/2 = Gamma(d+1) Gamma(d/2) / (4 Gamma(3d/2))), with exact rational values f(1)=1, f(2)=1/2, f(3)=8/35 and f(4)=1/10; in Lean these four values are entered as a table (70 f(d) = 70, 35, 16, 7) and not derived from the Gamma formula. (i) If the n x n grid with the componentwise product order has R(n) = (n(n+1)/2)^2 - n^2 strictly related pairs (a count entered as a definition in Lean, not derived from a poset), then 4 R(n) = n^2 (n-1)(n+3), the ordering fraction is r = (n+3)/(2(n+1)) for all n >= 2 with r(n) - 1/2 = 1/(n+1), the values for n=2..6 are 5/6, 3/4, 7/10, 2/3, 9/14, and r(2) = 5/6 equals the exactly computed r(C2) of the diamond. This is an observation about a lattice, not an instance of the sprinkling theorem. (ii) An exact nearest-dimension selector over d in {1,2,3,4} with tie reporting is defined and checked on the six inputs 5/6, 3/4, 7/10, 1/2, 8/35, 1/10, giving [1], [1,2] (an exact tie), [2], [2], [3], [4]. (iii) The Hasse covering relation of any FiniteStrictPoset is contained in every subrelation E of the order such that every related pair is in E or has an intermediate element (one half of "unique transitive reduction"); C1 has 2 links and C2 has 4; the Mobius tables c1_mu and c2_mu of CausalOrder.lean satisfy the Mobius recursion and c2_mu(d0,d3)=1.

Obligation: Not proved in Lean: that the n x n grid poset (a FiniteStrictPoset on n^2 points) has R(n) strictly related pairs, so (i) is arithmetic on a posited count cross-checked against the diamond only at n=2; the derivation of f(d) from the Gamma-function formula; correctness of the nearest-dimension selector beyond the six listed inputs; that the Hasse relation itself generates the order and is the minimal such relation. Everything is rational arithmetic on named finite posets. The dimension estimator is a heuristic for sprinklings; the finite estimate on a small poset carries no manifold statement.

### TFQ-2204 Imported: entropy of a boundary region equals minimal surface area over 4G

- UUID: `602d7a44-e877-5fde-956c-e06842080c7e`

Imported formula, as the source states it at leading order in Newton's constant: S(A) = Area(minimal surface anchored on the boundary of A) / (4 G). It presupposes the von Neumann entropy of a boundary reduced state on a continuum Hilbert space and the area of a surface in a bulk geometry. The repository has an exact von Neumann entropy dichotomy for algebraic spectra and an exact rational Regge area proxy that is not the Einstein-Hilbert action; neither is a minimal-surface area in a bulk geometry. Narrowed in Lean 4 and an independent Python verifier to three exact finite/rational algebraic shadows and scope fences: (1) over Q, substituting the regulated AdS_3 geodesic length 2 R_AdS * logFactor into rtLeadingEntropy(area, G_N) = area / (4 G_N) reproduces the 2D CFT Calabrese-Cardy coefficient (c / 3) * logFactor under the Brown-Henneaux relation c = 3 R_AdS / (2 G_N^(3)) and eliminates both bulk couplings in S_A / c = logFactor / 3, while submodular surface pasting yields Strong Subadditivity S(ABC) + S(B) <= S(AB) + S(BC) and all 380 proper contiguous boundary intervals of the 20-qubit 6-pentagon HaPPY patch satisfy complement symmetry A <-> A^c; (2) under BakerCitedInput (EntropyDichotomy.lean), no mixed algebraic spectrum can have natural-log von Neumann entropy equal to a rational RT ratio area / (4 G_N), equality holds at G_N > 0 iff the state is pure and area = 0, and stabilizer bit counts require dividing by log 2; and (3) on the orthogonal_pentatope chart of TFQ-0100, the 6 right-triangle hinges have Cayley-Menger squared area 1/4 and the 4 equilateral-triangle hinges have squared area 3/4 (total 9/2) with no rational linear area A in Q satisfying A^2 = 3/4, the flat-chart Regge proxy (kappa = 0) vanishes identically whereas all 380 HaPPY intervals satisfy 1 <= S(A) <= mincut(A), and under length rescaling L -> lam * L the Regge proxy scales as lam^4 against lam^2 for 2-surface area and lam^0 for bond counts.

Obligation: No source supplies a dictionary from the repository's finite areas to the surface areas of the formula; under BakerCitedInput mixed algebraic spectra have transcendental natural-log entropy, and the TFQ-0100 rational Regge proxy scales as lam^4 and vanishes on flat charts.

### TFQ-2208 Finite target: the five-qubit code gives a six-leg perfect tensor

- UUID: `400b1aba-b746-519a-a66c-9991879f6699`
- Parent: `TFQ-2207`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `ADS-FIVE-QUBIT-PERFECT-TENSOR-TARGET`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/32_ads_cft/tfq_2208_ads_five_qubit_perfect_tensor_target.md)

Formalized finite statement. The [[5,1,3]] code of Laflamme, Miquel, Paz and Zurek has stabilizer generators XZZXI, IXZZX, XIXZZ, ZXIXZ and logical operators XXXXX and ZZZZZ. Its Choi state is the six-qubit stabilizer state with generators g tensor I (four of them), XXXXX tensor X and ZZZZZ tensor Z. Checked in Lean 4 on Pauli operators modulo phase (GF(2) symplectic vectors): the six generators pairwise commute and generate a group of 64 distinct elements, with weight distribution 1 element of weight 0, 45 of weight 4 and 18 of weight 6 (the hexacode six-qubit state), so every non-identity element has weight at least 4, which is the perfect-tensor condition (every bipartition with at most three legs on one side has a maximally mixed marginal); for all twenty 3|3 bipartitions the stabilizer subgroup supported on one side is trivial, so the entropy is 3 bits by the stabilizer formula S(A) = |A| - log2 |G_A|; and in the five-qubit code the normalizer of the 16-element stabilizer has order 64 and its 48 elements outside the stabilizer (the nontrivial logical operators, modulo phase) have minimum weight 3. The reading of weights and local stabilizer subgroups as marginals and entropies is the standard stabilizer-formalism dictionary and is not formalised on density matrices.

Obligation: Checked in Lean 4 by exhaustive GF(2) symplectic enumeration over the 64-element stabilizer group, the 20 bipartitions and the 1024-element five-qubit Pauli group. A finite stabilizer enumeration is not a statement about AdS/CFT.

### TFQ-2209 Finite target: boundary entropies of a six-tensor patch against minimal cuts

- UUID: `e13ff21c-928d-51dd-92d2-b16df4265009`
- Parent: `TFQ-2208`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `ADS-HAPPY-ENTROPY-MINCUT-TARGET`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/32_ads_cft/tfq_2209_ads_happy_entropy_mincut_target.md)

Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 for a hand-encoded model. Contract six copies of the six-leg perfect tensor on the {5,4} pentagon tiling: one central tensor and its five edge-neighbours, which are not adjacent to each other, so the patch has 20 dangling boundary legs (4 per outer tensor) and 6 bulk legs, every bulk leg fixed in the logical zero state. In Lean the 20-qubit boundary stabilizer is given by 20 explicit generators (15 local to the five outer blocks and 5 pushed through the internal bonds from the central tensor): they pairwise commute and have full GF(2) rank 20. For all 380 proper contiguous boundary intervals A (20 starting positions, lengths 1 to 19), with S(A) = rank(G restricted to A) - |A| in bits and mincut(A) the minimal number of bonds cut separating A from its complement in the six-tensor star graph: S(A) <= mincut(A) on all 380 intervals, S(A) = mincut(A) on exactly 340 intervals, and S(A) = mincut(A) - 1 on exactly 40. The Ryu-Takayanagi equality therefore fails on this patch for 40 intervals; it is not a statement that holds for every region.

Obligation: Not proved in Lean: that the 20 explicit generators are the boundary stabilizer of the contracted six-tensor network with bulk legs fixed at logical zero (they are entered by hand from the pushing rules of the code generators); that mincut as computed (a minimum over side assignments of the six tensors) is the minimal curve cut in the planar dual; the list of the 40 intervals where equality fails (only the counts are stated). The correspondence to a continuum minimal-surface area is the imported formula and is not part of the target.

### TFQ-2210 Finite target: logical operators of the five-qubit code live on any three qubits

- UUID: `4098496c-a23a-5e32-bd93-c2b8dfdceca8`

Formalized finite statement. For the [[5,1,3]] code, each of the ten 3-qubit subsets T of physical qubits supports a representative of each of the three nontrivial logical classes (the cosets of the stabilizer by XXXXX, ZZZZZ and YYYYY, the product class), and no 2-qubit subset supports a representative of any of them. Equivalent statement also checked in Lean 4: all 105 non-identity Pauli errors of weight 1 or 2 anticommute with a stabilizer generator, so none lies in the normalizer and erasure of any two qubits is correctable (the Knill-Laflamme condition). All operators are Pauli operators modulo phase. This is the smallest exact instance of the subregion-reconstruction picture of bulk operators.

Obligation: Checked in Lean 4 over the 16-element stabilizer, its three logical cosets, all 10 triples, all 10 pairs and all 105 low-weight Pauli errors. The identification with bulk operator reconstruction in AdS/CFT is the imported picture of the source.

### TFQ-2212 Gap: finite code checks are not a derivation of AdS/CFT

- UUID: `a6188d7a-9c6f-5049-9106-5b47e953fae7`

No source read for this change derives AdS/CFT, or its continuum entropy formula, from a finite stabilizer-code tensor network. The HaPPY codes are discrete kinematic models of the bulk-to-boundary map on a hyperbolic tiling with no Lorentzian time, no dynamics, no gravitational action and no large-N limit. Narrowed in Lean 4 and an independent Python verifier to three exact non-equivalence fences: (1) every stabilizer reduced state has flat Renyi spectrum S_n / S_1 = 1, whereas a 2D CFT single interval has Calabrese-Cardy / Ryu-Takayanagi Renyi ratio cftRenyiFactor(n) = (1 + 1/n)/2, yielding a strictly positive defect ((n - 1)/(2n)) * S_1 > 0 for all n > 1 and S_1 > 0; (2) on the 20-qubit boundary state of the 6-pentagon {5,4} HaPPY patch (with bulk legs fixed in |0_L>), all 280 contiguous intervals of lengths 1..7 and 13..19 satisfy S(A) = mincut(A), whereas lengths 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 exhibit 5, 10, 10, 10, 5 strict Ryu-Takayanagi deficits (S(A) = mincut(A) - 1, summing to 40), including the explicit 5-fold rotational orbit start = 4*k + 2 at len = 8 and its complement len = 12 (S = 4 < 5 = mincut); and (3) disconnected boundary regions exhibit discrete integer mutual-information jumps (0, 0, 3, 1 bits) while for nBulk < nBdry the bulk code subspace 2^{nBulk} has strictly positive orthogonal codimension 2^{nBdry} - 2^{nBulk} > 0 (30, 1048512, 33552384 for 1, 6, and 11 pentagons).

Obligation: Recorded as an explicit non-claim and non-equivalence fence so that finite stabilizer-code checks are not read as evidence for continuum AdS/CFT; Lorentzian time evolution, non-flat entanglement spectra, sub-AdS locality, and continuum gravitational dynamics remain open.

### TFQ-2301 Rovelli and Smolin 1995: spin networks and quantum gravity

- UUID: `b27e8a21-0118-521b-9ebd-4748a46f1835`
- Parent: `TFQ-2300`
- Status: `SOURCE_RECORD`
- DAG node: `LQG-SPIN-NETWORK-KINEMATICS-SOURCE`

Rovelli and Smolin (1995, arXiv:gr-qc/9505006, Phys. Rev. D 52, 5743) construct an independent basis of states in both the loop representation (Section 3 pp. 12-16) and the SU(2) connection representation (Section 4 pp. 17-24) that solves the SU(2) Mandelstam identities (Section 2 eq. (21) and conditions i-ii p. 12), labelled by imbedded graphs whose edges carry SU(2) representations (twice-spins p_l) and whose higher-valence vertices carry virtual trivalent trees/intertwiners (Appendix A pp. 36-38), and show in Section 6 (pp. 26-29) that these spin-network states are orthonormal with respect to the Ashtekar-Lewandowski Haar measure. This node records the paper as published.

Obligation: Record only. Audited against the full text of arXiv:gr-qc/9505006 on 2026-10-22.

### TFQ-2303 Rovelli-Smolin 1995 and Ashtekar-Lewandowski 1997: area and volume spectra

- UUID: `02729703-f7d9-5686-9dac-b26b001fea39`
- Parent: `TFQ-2301`
- Status: `SOURCE_RECORD`
- DAG node: `LQG-AREA-VOLUME-SPECTRA-SOURCE`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/33_loop_quantum_gravity/tfq_2303_lqg_area_volume_spectra_source.md)

Rovelli and Smolin (1995, arXiv:gr-qc/9411005, Section 1 eqs. (1)-(2) p. 4 and Section 4 eqs. (47)-(48) p. 28) and Ashtekar and Lewandowski (1997, arXiv:gr-qc/9602046, Section 3.3 eq. (3.20) p. 16 and Section 4.1 eqs. (4.7)-(4.9), (4.12) pp. 18-19) compute discrete spectra for loop-quantum-gravity area (and volume) operators. In the convention {A_a^i(x), E_j^b(y)} = G delta_a^b delta_j^i delta^3(x,y) used in both papers, the general area eigenvalue is (l_P^2 / 2) sum_v sqrt(2 j_v^(d)(j_v^(d)+1) + 2 j_v^(u)(j_v^(u)+1) - j_v^(d+u)(j_v^(d+u)+1)) (eq. (4.9) of gr-qc/9602046), which for simple transverse punctures without tangential edges (j^(d)=j^(u)=j_i, j^(d+u)=0) equals l_P^2 sum_i sqrt(j_i(j_i+1)) = (l_P^2 / 2) sum_i sqrt(p_i(p_i+2)) with p_i = 2 j_i (eq. (2) and eq. (47) of gr-qc/9411005; eq. (4.12) of gr-qc/9602046); as Ashtekar and Lewandowski note in Section 3.3 footnote 6 (p. 16) and Engle et al. write in arXiv:0711.0146 Section V eq. (36) (p. 11), restoring the 8 pi G gamma factor from the gravitational action and Barbero-Immirzi parameter gamma multiplies this spectrum by 8 pi gamma, giving 8 pi gamma l_P^2 sum_i sqrt(j_i(j_i+1)). (The nonzero trivalent volume formula in eq. (1) and eq. (37) of gr-qc/9411005 was corrected in the erratum Nucl. Phys. B 456 (1995) 753, where trivalent vertices have zero volume.) This node records both papers and their normalization conventions.

Obligation: Record only. Both normalization conventions (l_P^2 vs 8 pi gamma l_P^2, per Ashtekar-Lewandowski Section 3.3 footnote 6 p. 16) and the general vertex-puncture formula (eq. (4.9) p. 18) were audited against the papers on 2026-10-22.

### TFQ-2304 Finite target: exact area levels as sums of square roots

- UUID: `9f7ae529-f14a-5564-8359-5e0db261c9b3`
- Parent: `TFQ-2303`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `LQG-AREA-SPECTRUM-EXACT-TARGET`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/33_loop_quantum_gravity/tfq_2304_lqg_area_spectrum_exact_target.md)

Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the formal radical basis. With the dimensionless area a = sum over punctures of sqrt(j(j+1)) for spins j in {1/2, 1, 3/2, 2, 5/2, 3}, each term is c_j sqrt(s_j) with squarefree radicand s_j in {2, 3, 6, 15, 35}: sqrt(3)/2, sqrt(2), sqrt(15)/2, sqrt(6), sqrt(35)/2 and 2 sqrt(3) for j = 1/2, 1, 3/2, 2, 5/2, 3 (radicands 3, 2, 15, 6, 35, 3); Lean checks k(k+2) = m_k^2 d_k with d_k squarefree for the twice-spins k = 1..6, and holds each term as a vector in the formal Q-module on the basis (sqrt2, sqrt3, sqrt6, sqrt15, sqrt35)/2. On that module: (i) the 210 puncture multisets of size at most 4 (the empty one and 209 nonempty ones) have 209 distinct reduced vectors, the zero vector included (208 nonzero); (ii) the unique collision is one puncture of spin 3 with four punctures of spin 1/2 (2 sqrt(3) = 4 x sqrt(3)/2); (iii) for a single puncture the squared area j(j+1) = k(k+2)/4 is at least 3/4, strictly increasing in k, with minimum 3/4 at j = 1/2 (area sqrt(3)/2).

Obligation: Not proved in Lean: that the formal vector is the real area (no real square root occurs in the module) and that two multisets have equal real area if and only if their vectors agree, which needs the linear independence over Q of sqrt(2), sqrt(3), sqrt(6), sqrt(15), sqrt(35) (stated in the module header, not a Lean theorem); the agreement of the hand-entered punctureArea table with the m_k, d_k table beyond inspection; the minimum over multisets of several punctures (only single punctures). The physical constant, the Immirzi parameter and the gauge-invariance constraint on admissible puncture lists are not part of the target.

### TFQ-2305 Ponzano and Regge 1968: semiclassical limit of Racah coefficients

- UUID: `c685d34a-2b12-57df-9673-e570bb2f1b67`

Ponzano and Regge (1968) give the leading asymptotic form of the 6j symbol (Racah coefficient) for large spins, with separate forms for the classically allowed and forbidden regions, and introduce a state sum for three-dimensional gravity whose phase matches the Regge action of a tetrahedron. The formula was reached by conjecture and numerical checks. This node records the chapter by title and publication details.

Obligation: Record only. The 1968 chapter has no arXiv record and is not held in the checkout; its asymptotic formula is verified in Roberts (1999, arXiv:math-ph/9812013 Theorem 1 p. 22 and Section 6.1 p. 61).

### TFQ-2306 Roberts 1999: classical 6j symbols and the tetrahedron

- UUID: `e9986f1e-f2ae-5a6c-81af-234693109e7c`
- Parent: `TFQ-2305`
- Status: `SOURCE_RECORD`
- DAG node: `LQG-ROBERTS-1999-SOURCE`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/33_loop_quantum_gravity/tfq_2306_lqg_roberts_1999_source.md)

Roberts (1999, arXiv:math-ph/9812013, Section 1 Theorem 1 eq. (2) p. 22 and Section 6.1 eqs. (12)-(13) p. 61) establishes by geometric quantization of the 8-sphere and stationary phase on the symplectic reduction that for an admissible 6-tuple of integers a, b, c, d, e, f (where a = 2j labels the (a+1)-dimensional irreducible representation of SU(2)) whose side lengths form a non-degenerate Euclidean tetrahedron tau of positive volume V(tau) > 0 and exterior dihedral angles theta_r, the rescaled 6j symbol {ka, kb, kc; kd, ke, kf} has the k -> infinity asymptotic expansion sqrt(2 / (3 pi V(tau) k^3)) cos(sum_{r=1}^6 (k a_r + 1) theta_r / 2 + pi/4) + O(k^{-5/2}). Since a tetrahedron of side lengths j_r = a_r/2 has volume V_j = V(tau)/8, substituting 2 / (3 pi V(tau)) = 1 / (12 pi V_j) and (a_r + 1)/2 = j_r + 1/2 recovers the Ponzano-Regge prefactor (12 pi V_j)^{-1/2}. This node records the paper's theorem.

Obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:math-ph/9812013 Theorem 1 eq. (2) p. 22 and Section 6.1 eqs. (12)-(13) p. 61 on 2026-10-22.

### TFQ-2307 Imported: Ponzano-Regge asymptotics of the 6j symbol

- UUID: `48d886d1-8ad2-572b-8ddf-a23c60caa4b2`
- Parent: `TFQ-2306`
- Status: `IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`

Imported asymptotic form, audited against Roberts (1999, arXiv:math-ph/9812013, Theorem 1 eq. (2) p. 22 and Section 6.1 eqs. (12)-(13) p. 61): for large spins with edge lengths l_r = j_r + 1/2 = (a_r + 1)/2 (where a_r = 2 j_r), when the six lengths bound a non-degenerate Euclidean tetrahedron of positive volume V > 0 and exterior dihedral angles theta_r, the 6j symbol behaves asymptotically as (12 pi V)^{-1/2} cos(sum_{r=1}^6 (j_r + 1/2) theta_r + pi/4) (equivalently sqrt(2 / (3 pi V(a))) cos(sum_{r=1}^6 (a_r + 1) theta_r / 2 + pi/4) where V(a) = 8 V is the volume for side lengths a_r = 2 j_r), and decays exponentially when the Cayley-Menger squared volume is negative (Lorentzian tetrahedron, Section 6.2 p. 62). The phase is the Regge action of the tetrahedron.

Obligation: The asymptotic statement is a limit of real-valued quantities; the repository's exact finite targets do not establish a limit.

### TFQ-2308 Finite target: exact classical 6j symbols, orthogonality and the Biedenharn-Elliott identity

- UUID: `53a2a9cc-9dbd-5f2b-b1b4-7072180167ec`
- Parent: `TFQ-2305`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `LQG-6J-EXACT-AND-PENTAGON-TARGET`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/33_loop_quantum_gravity/tfq_2308_lqg_6j_exact_and_pentagon_target.md)

Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. The Wigner 6j symbol with twice-spins at most 6 is S sqrt(P), where S is Racah's single-sum factor, computed with exact integer factorials, and P is the product of four rational triangle factors; Lean defines the rational square W^2 = S^2 P (sixJSquaredRat) in this way. Checks: (i) the signed Racah factor S is invariant under the four generators of the 24 tetrahedral symmetries (the column swaps 12 and 23 and the double row flips on columns 12 and 23) for all 3,418 admissible 6-tuples with twice-spins at most 6 (the invariance of P under the symmetries is evident, since they permute its four triangle factors, but is not part of the Lean check); (ii) the orthogonality relation sum over x of (x+1)(y+1) {a b x; c d y}{a b x; c d y'} = delta(y,y') in twice-spin labels, for the 1,928 admissible tuples (a,b,c,d,y,y') whose labels and whose intermediate twice-spin x all lie at or below 6; (iii) the Biedenharn-Elliott (pentagon) identity for all 814 admissible 9-tuples with twice-spins at most 3, and for four explicit instances with twice-spins up to 6 (all labels 2; labels 3 with p=q=r=2; (a,b,c,d,e,f,p,q,r) = (4,2,3,3,2,4,3,3,2); and (6,0,6,0,6,0,6,6,6)). Exact arithmetic in the rationals with one square root per symbol.

Obligation: Not proved in Lean: the Biedenharn-Elliott identity exhaustively for twice-spins 4 to 6 (four instances only); orthogonality for tuples whose intermediate range exceeds twice-spin 6; invariance of P, W^2 and the signed symbol under the symmetry generators, and invariance under the whole group (the closure of the tuple set under the generators is not stated). Exact enumeration with big integers. The classical 6j is not the q-deformed 6j at level 2 recorded in TFQ-0105; the q to 1 limit is not part of the target.

### TFQ-2314 Imported: EPRL-FK vertex amplitude for four-dimensional gravity

- UUID: `6bb920ad-676d-55e3-8b2f-06375d0d50ee`
- Parent: `TFQ-2312`
- Status: `IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`
- DAG node: `LQG-EPRL-VERTEX-IMPORT`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/33_loop_quantum_gravity/tfq_2314_lqg_eprl_vertex_import.md)

For rational gamma and rational k, the imported Euclidean labels are j+ = |1 + gamma| k / 2 and j- = |1 - gamma| k / 2. When 0 < gamma < 1 they equal (1 + gamma) k / 2 and (1 - gamma) k / 2, their sum is k, and their difference is gamma k. When gamma > 1 they equal (1 + gamma) k / 2 and (gamma - 1) k / 2, their difference is k, and their sum is gamma k. At gamma = 1/2 and k = 2 the labels are 3/2 and 1/2, the sum is 2, and the difference is 1, which is not 2. At gamma = 3 and k = 2 the labels are 4 and 2, the difference is 2, and the sum is 6, which is not 2. At gamma = 1 and k = 2 the labels are 2 and 0, and both the sum and the difference equal 2. The imported Lorentzian pair is (n, rho) = (2 k, 2 gamma k), with rho = gamma n = 2 gamma (n / 2). At gamma = 1/2 and k = 2 this pair is (4, 2), the index j = n / 2 equals 2, and gamma j equals 1, so rho = 2 gamma j rather than gamma j. The number of unordered pairs among five indices is 10. A Spin(4) 15j contraction, booster factors, a continuum Lie-group representation, a spin-network boundary space, a sum over spins, a continuum limit, a semiclassical limit, and a cosmological constant stay imported and are not constructed. The finite cyclotomic amplitudes named by TFQ-0198 are not identified with an EPRL-FK vertex.

Obligation: The checked identities are rational arithmetic for the imported labels j+ = |1 + gamma| k / 2 and j- = |1 - gamma| k / 2, the pair (n, rho) = (2 k, 2 gamma k), and the count of 10 unordered pairs among five indices. They are not a Spin(4) 15j symbol, not a booster contraction, and not a continuum, semiclassical, or cosmological-constant limit. No source maps the finite cyclotomic amplitudes to the EPRL-FK amplitude.

## GENESIS_TO_HIGHER

### TFQ-2400 Finite semi-simplicial or globular shadow of Genesis admission

- UUID: `b6bc4fd0-1df2-5665-9d37-42402d1e7b89`
- Parent: `TFQ-0481`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `GTH-SHADOW`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/34_genesis_to_higher/tfq_2400_gth_shadow.md)

No construction turns PGW-GO-ADMISSION-GATE into a finite semi-simplicial set or a finite globular set. That gate keeps a two-valued admission record with a reached result: reaching leaves not-admitted, and admission is not one of the four kinds of change. A finite semi-simplicial set of dimension at most N is finite sets X_0, ..., X_N and face maps d_i from X_n to X_{n-1} such that d_i composed with d_j equals d_{j-1} composed with d_i whenever i < j. It carries no degeneracy maps. A finite globular set is finite sets with source and target maps s, t from X_{n+1} to X_n such that s composed with s equals s composed with t, and t composed with t equals t composed with s. Neither family is defined from the admission record.

Obligation: Missing parent construction: PGW-GO-ADMISSION-GATE is a two-valued admission record, and no source builds a finite semi-simplicial set or a finite globular set from it.

### TFQ-2401 Truncation: components, finite fundamental groupoid, finite n-type presentation

- UUID: `4469b8a8-1254-5df8-9da6-0d29c742b794`
- Parent: `TFQ-2400`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `GTH-TRUNC`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/34_genesis_to_higher/tfq_2401_gth_trunc.md)

Let a finite shadow be a finite semi-simplicial set or a finite globular set as in GTH-SHADOW. Its set of path components, pi_0, is the quotient of the 0-cells by the equivalence relation generated by finite 1-zigzags. Its finite fundamental groupoid has the 0-cells as objects and, as morphisms, equivalence classes of finite 1-paths, the equivalence being the one generated by the 2-cells when 2-cells are part of the shadow. A finite n-type presentation keeps cells and face data through dimension n and stops there. None of these quotients or presentations is constructed, because no shadow is constructed from the admission gate.

### TFQ-2402 Horn fillers of a finite shadow

- UUID: `c5980de6-3c2c-5a02-acd2-422d8ac51445`
- Parent: `TFQ-2401`
- Status: `OPEN_OBLIGATION`
- DAG node: `GTH-HORNS`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/34_genesis_to_higher/tfq_2402_gth_horns.md)

The horn Lambda^k[n] is the union of all faces of the standard n-simplex except the face opposite vertex k. The horn is inner when 0 < k < n and outer when k = 0 or k = n. A Kan condition asks for a filler of every horn. A quasicategory asks for a filler of every inner horn, in the sense of Joyal, Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra 175 (2002) 207-222. Which of these fillers a finite object derived from Genesis admission would have is open. No filler is exhibited and no counterexample is exhibited, because no such finite object is constructed.

Obligation: Which horns would have fillers is open. There is no object of which a filler or a missing filler could be shown.

### TFQ-2404 Imported: a univalent universe is not finite

- UUID: `b40ff37b-4f62-5a02-9915-49457792dbac`
- Parent: `TFQ-2403`
- Status: `IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`
- DAG node: `GTH-IMPORT-UNIVALENT-UNIVERSE`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/34_genesis_to_higher/tfq_2404_gth_import_univalent_universe.md)

Assumed, and not derived from Genesis admission or from any finite model: a univalent universe in the sense of the Homotopy Type Theory book (The Univalent Foundations Program, Institute for Advanced Study, 2013), a type U together with a map from the identity type Id_U(A, B) to the type of equivalences between A and B that is itself an equivalence. Such a universe is not a finite set and is not a finite semi-simplicial set of bounded dimension. A finite model of a fragment with identity types, were one later defined, would be only an approximation of this assumption: the assumption is an infinite object, and the finite model would not contain it.

Obligation: The assumption is a univalent universe. It is not finite, it is not derived, and any finite identity-type model is only an approximation of it.

### TFQ-2405 Imported: an infinity-groupoid is not finite

An infinity-groupoid has cells in every finite dimension. It is not a finite semi-simplicial set of bounded dimension. A finite n-type presentation is only an approximation of this assumption: it stops at a fixed dimension and does not supply fillers in all higher dimensions.

Obligation: The assumption is an infinity-groupoid (Kan complex, fillers for every horn). It is not finite, it is not derived, and a finite n-type is only an approximation.

### TFQ-2406 Imported: an (infinity,1)-category is not finite

Joyal, Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra 175 (2002) 207-222, isolates that inner-horn condition and its relation to Kan complexes. Boardman and Vogt, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 347 (1973), introduced the weak Kan complexes of which this is the later name. Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, arXiv:math/0608040, develops the theory. An (infinity,1)-category is not a finite semi-simplicial set. A finite inner-horn condition on a finite complex, were one stated, would be only an approximation of this assumption.

Obligation: The assumption is an (infinity,1)-category (inner horn fillers). It is not finite, it is not derived, and a finite inner-horn condition is only an approximation.

### TFQ-2411 Goedel-Rosser and Tarski limit

- UUID: `f29d7a07-2d64-5106-9467-9253a955987e`
- Parent: `TFQ-2410`
- Status: `PROVED_PROSE`
- DAG node: `GTH-LANG-LIMITS`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/34_genesis_to_higher/tfq_2411_gth_lang_limits.md)

Let S be a theory in classical first-order logic with a primitive recursive coding of its syntax. Write code(psi) for the code of a sentence psi and num(n) for the numeral of a natural number n. Assume (i) consistency: there is no sentence psi such that S derives both psi and the negation of psi. Assume (ii) a primitive recursive relation Proof such that psi is a theorem of S exactly when Proof(p, code(psi)) holds for some natural number p, and Proof is represented at standard numerals: for all natural numbers p and s, S derives the sentence expressing Proof(num(p), num(s)) when the relation holds and derives its negation when the relation fails. Assume (iii) that S derives every true Delta_0 sentence of this coding; that the substitution function subst, sending the code of a formula with one free variable and a number n to the code of the sentence obtained by substituting num(n) for that variable, is represented in S; that the primitive recursive function neg on codes, with neg(code(psi)) equal to code(the negation of psi), is represented in S; and that for each standard natural number n, S derives both that every w with w < num(n) equals one of num(0), ..., num(n-1), and that every w satisfies w < num(n) or w = num(n) or num(n) < w. Then there is a sentence phi such that S derives neither phi nor the negation of phi. The diagonal lemma from representation of subst supplies, for the negation of the Rosser formula RosserProv(v) given by existence of a u such that Proof(u, v) and such that Proof(w, neg(v)) fails for every w < u, a sentence phi such that S derives the biconditional of phi and the negation of RosserProv(num(code(phi))). If S derives phi, a standard derivation code p, clause (i), numeral-wise representation of Proof, and the schema that every number below num(p) equals one of num(0), ..., num(p-1), yield a derivation of RosserProv(num(code(phi))) and then of the negation of phi. If S derives the negation of phi, a least standard derivation code q of that negation, numeral-wise representation of Proof, the same bounded schema at q, and the schema that every number is below num(q), equal to num(q), or above num(q), yield a derivation of the negation of RosserProv(num(code(phi))) and then of phi. Either case contradicts (i). Separately, drop (i) and (ii) and keep (iii): if a formula Tr(x) is such that S derives the biconditional of Tr(num(code(psi))) and psi for every sentence psi, the same diagonal lemma applied to the negation of Tr supplies a sentence lambda for which those biconditionals yield a derivation of both lambda and its negation, so S is inconsistent. Both conclusions use only the hypotheses just stated and classical first-order logic.

Obligation: The two limit statements are conditional on the hypotheses in the statement. The priced admission language is not defined and is not shown to meet (i), (ii) or (iii). Nothing is formalised in Lean. Admitting a later theory is a priced import record, not a derivation from the core.

### TFQ-2500 Observer tuple for empirical claims

- UUID: `8cbf37ea-1102-540a-ad9c-7bb634505489`
- Parent: `TFQ-0553`
- Status: `DEFINITION`
- DAG node: `OPS-OBSERVER-TUPLE`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/35_foc035_observer_presheaf/tfq_2500_ops_observer_tuple.md)

Definition A1 of the source note. Fix a finite set M of measurements with finite outcome sets and a cover C of M by maximal contexts, and write E(U) for the set of outcome assignments on U. An observer tuple is O = (K, Adm, norm, Term, L). K = (M, C, E). Adm is the convex hull conv(A) of the vectors (delta_g restricted to C) over all contexts C, for g in E(M). The norm is the l1 norm on the stacked context distributions. Term maps the defect and the claim to a status: defect 0 gives ExactRepair, defect above 0 with a support-level global section gives ClosedResidual, and otherwise OpenObstruction. L is the diagnostic layer. The defect of a claim e = (e_C), one distribution per context, is Delta_O(e) = min over p in Adm of the l1 norm of (e - p). The five components are a projection of the four packets of WDP chapter 10 (presentation, memory, evaluator, policy) and of the chapter 15 grade. The monograph defines no five-tuple of its own; the ledger row records a search for "5-tuple" that returned nothing.

Obligation: A reading of WDP-CH10-D01 to D04, not a derivation. WDP chapter 15 has no node in this graph, so the layer component has no repository node to attach to. No source relates the L1 observer axioms H1 to H5 to this five-component tuple.

### TFQ-2501 Pushforward of natural-number measures is functorial (Lean)

- UUID: `cc8966bf-4d86-5fbf-a65c-97a119e27458`
- Parent: `TFQ-1046`
- Status: `PROVED_LEAN`
- DAG node: `OPS-PUSHFORWARD-FUNCTOR-LEAN`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/35_foc035_observer_presheaf/tfq_2501_ops_pushforward_functor_lean.md)

In Lean (LggrFiniteResults), a finitely supported measure with natural-number weights is a list of (value, weight) pairs, and pushforward along f maps each value by f and keeps its weight. Then: push of the identity is the identity (push_id); push along g after f equals push along the composite (push_comp); total mass is unchanged (mass_push); and the weight at b of push f p equals the mass of the entries of p whose image is b (weightAt_push). The note reads marginalisation of a context distribution as such a pushforward along the restriction map, so these are the identity and composition laws of the functor from the opposite of the context poset to probability vectors (Lemma B2). That reading is not a Lean statement. Not covered: rational weights, normalisation to probability vectors, the context poset, and the Rust types. The ledger row states the same narrowing.

Obligation: The Lean statement is the narrowed one above. The functor over rational probability vectors is proved in prose in the note (Lemma B2) and its instances on the PR box and the noisy PR boxes are recomputed by the independent check, which does not test the Lean statement. Independently replayed with Lean 4.35.0; the source-bound axiom receipt is dag/research/foc035_observer_presheaf_lean_replay.json.

### TFQ-2502 Parity cycles: holonomy and global sections (Lean)

- UUID: `f4173ff6-cd81-51c4-8dc8-cfa695f3425d`
- Parent: `TFQ-1046`
- Status: `PROVED_LEAN`
- DAG node: `OPS-PARITY-HOLONOMY-LEAN`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/35_foc035_observer_presheaf/tfq_2502_ops_parity_holonomy_lean.md)

In Lean (LggrFiniteResults), take a length n > 0 and edge parities b : Nat -> Bool. Let holonomy b k be the exclusive or of b 0, ..., b (k-1), and call g a section when, for every i < n, the exclusive or of g i and g ((i+1) mod n) equals b i. Then (section_exists_iff_holonomy_zero) a section exists if and only if holonomy b n = false. Further (no_joint_measure_when_holonomy_one), if holonomy b n = true then no finitely supported natural-weight measure on assignments Nat -> Bool with positive total mass has, for every i < n, zero pushforward weight on every pair of values (g i, g ((i+1) mod n)) whose exclusive or differs from b i. These are the clause "G(e) is nonempty iff the holonomy h is 0" and the clause "holonomy 1 forbids a positive-mass joint measure with parity-supported marginals" of Proposition B6. Not in Lean: the arc-cover clause, the noncontextual-fraction clause and the Cech-cohomology reading.

Obligation: The Lean statement is the narrowed one above; no Lean statement mentions a nerve, a cohomology class or the noncontextual fraction. Independently replayed with Lean 4.35.0; the source-bound axiom receipt is dag/research/foc035_observer_presheaf_lean_replay.json.

### TFQ-2503 Global section, convex hull and noncontextual fraction 1

Proposition B3(1). For an empirical model e = (e_C) on a finite scenario, let A be the matrix whose column g, for g in E(M), is the stacked vector of the point masses of g restricted to each context, and let NCF(e) = max of the sum of lambda_g over lambda >= 0 with A lambda <= e. Then these are equivalent: e has a global section (a probability vector d on E(M) with marginal e_C on every context C); e lies in conv(A); NCF(e) = 1. This is the local-hidden-variable condition. Instances recomputed exactly: the mixture (1/2)(delta_g1 + delta_g2), with g1 = (0,0,0,0) and g2 = (1,0,0,1) on (a, a', b, b'), has NCF 1; the noisy PR box (1 - lam) PR + lam U at lam = 1/2 has NCF 1 and a distribution as a global section.

Proposition B3(3). Write G(e) for the set of g in E(M) with e_C(g restricted to C) > 0 for every context C. Then e is strongly contextual (G(e) is empty) if and only if NCF(e) = 0: if lambda_g > 0 is feasible then e_C(g|C) >= lambda_g > 0 for every C, so g is in G(e); conversely g in G(e) makes lambda = (min over C of e_C(g|C)) delta_g feasible with positive weight. The four parity constraints x_a + x_b = 0, x_a + x_b' = 0, x_a' + x_b = 0 and x_a' + x_b' = 1 sum to 0 = 1 modulo 2, so none of the 16 assignments satisfies all.

### TFQ-2506 Descent over the maximal cover never fails to glue

- UUID: `bbd9195f-c6d0-5e08-8014-2686a3ae579a`

Proposition B4(1). Let S(U) be the set of assignments s on U whose restriction to every maximal context C inside U lies in the support of e_C; then S(M) = G(e). Over the cover of M by its maximal contexts, every matching family (s_C in S(C), agreeing on overlaps) glues to exactly one element of S(M). So a descent classifier on that cover reports no NoGlobalExtension, its fibers are in bijection with G(e), and strong contextuality appears as zero matching families, not as a failed gluing. Instances recomputed exactly: the PR box has 0 matching families; the noisy PR box at lam = 1/2 has 16, each with exactly one gluing.

- Paper: [derivation](derivations/35_foc035_observer_presheaf/tfq_2511_ops_parity_cycle_descent_ncf.md)

For n = 3, 4, 5 and every one of the 2^n parity-target vectors t on the n-cycle of binary measurements (contexts {m_i, m_(i+1 mod n)}, each distribution uniform on the two pairs with x_i xor x_(i+1) = t_i), let h be the exclusive or of the t_i. Then |G| is 2 if h = 0 and 0 if h = 1; the arc cover {m_0, ..., m_(n-2)}, {m_1, ..., m_(n-1)} has exactly 2 matching families, both with one gluing if h = 0 and both without a gluing if h = 1; and NCF is 1 if h = 0 and 0 if h = 1. That is 8 + 16 + 32 = 56 cases.

Obligation: Finite cases n = 3, 4, 5 only. The two clauses proved in Lean for every n are in node OPS-PARITY-HOLONOMY-LEAN; the arc-cover and NCF clauses for general n are not claimed.

### TFQ-2512 No-signalling and signed global sections

- UUID: `911513ca-674d-5558-8c82-f06886b554bd`
- Parent: `TFQ-2503`

- Paper: [derivation](derivations/35_foc035_observer_presheaf/tfq_2512_ops_no_signalling_signed_section.md)

Assumed from Abramsky and Brandenburger (New Journal of Physics 13 (2011) 113036, arXiv:1102.0264), as the note cites it and does not prove it: an empirical model is no-signalling if and only if it has a signed global section, a function d on E(M) with values in Q, sum 1 and the given marginals. Instance recomputed exactly: the PR box, which is no-signalling, has a signed global section found by exact linear algebra, with sum 1, all 16 marginal equations satisfied and at least one negative entry.

Obligation: The equivalence is cited, not derived here. The instance covers one no-signalling model and says nothing about the converse direction or about other models.

### TFQ-2514 Vorob'ev: acyclic covers glue every no-signalling model

- UUID: `94ecea7e-2215-5473-9bfc-6e96863adbe7`
- Parent: `TFQ-2503`
- Status: `IMPORTED_ASSUMPTION`
- DAG node: `OPS-VOROBEV-THEOREM`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/35_foc035_observer_presheaf/tfq_2514_ops_vorobev_theorem.md)

Assumed from Vorob'ev (Theory of Probability and its Applications 7 (1962) 147-163, doi:10.1137/1107014), as the note states it: if the hypergraph (M, C) is GYO-acyclic (it reduces to nothing by removing ears and absorbed vertices, equivalently it has a join tree), then every no-signalling model has a global section given on a join tree T by d(g) = (product over C of e_C(g|C)) / (product over the edges (C, C') of T of e_(C intersect C')(g|C intersect C')), with 0/0 = 0. The note gives an induction sketch, not a full proof. The converse (for every non-acyclic hypergraph some no-signalling family has no global section) is not implemented; the PR box on the 4-cycle is one instance.

Obligation: Cited theorem with a proof sketch in the note only. Not formalised in Lean.

The GYO reduction empties the three-context path and the two-context path and does not empty the Bell 4-cycle or a triangle. This is one instance of the cited theorem, not a check of it.

### TFQ-2517 Conditional underdetermination of the receipt

- UUID: `9f3939b4-b0ae-56a7-b8eb-f7e62c4cdedd`
- Parent: `TFQ-2500`
- Status: `PROVED_PROSE`
- DAG node: `OPS-UNDERDETERMINATION`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/35_foc035_observer_presheaf/tfq_2517_ops_underdetermination.md)

Lemma A2. Let O' leave one of K, Adm, norm, Term undeclared, and require that an evaluation's receipt for a claim agree across every admissible completion of the undeclared component. Then no evaluation of O' meets that requirement: for each of the four components there are two admissible completions, agreeing elsewhere, whose receipts for one claim differ. Witnesses on the PR box (Bell scenario, parity targets 0, 0, 0, 1): K, the Bell cover gives defect 2 and the acyclic sub-cover {ab, ab'} gives defect 0; Adm, the noncontextual polytope gives 2 and the no-signalling polytope gives 0, because the PR box is no-signalling; norm, the l1 norm gives 2 and twice the l1 norm gives 4; Term, with defect 2 and empty global support the rule of the note gives OpenObstruction and the rule "defect below 3 gives ExactRepair" gives ExactRepair. The lemma does not say that no function from claims to receipts exists; any one completion defines a function. The layer has no row, because Definition A1 fixes it to diagnostic.

Obligation: The norm and Term rows are arithmetic on the defect 2, not receipts of a configurable evaluator: the Rust evaluator implements one norm and one terminal rule. The second receipt of the Adm row is proved, not computed by the Rust code. Not formalised in Lean.

### TFQ-2525 Axis 2 of the regress: the meta-carrier level

Axis 2. Let eval_n be the evaluator of a process on carrier K_n. The statement "eval_n is sound" relates eval_n to a standard of correctness for K_n; that standard is not an element of K_n, so the statement is a sentence of a carrier K_(n+1), and the output PASS of eval_n on it has no standing at K_(n+1) (ENC-0195, AuthorityEffect None). The level statement holds by construction of the carrier hierarchy. Imported: the strengthening by Tarski's undefinability theorem, which applies only when K_n interprets enough arithmetic, and the Genesis identifiers ENC-0118 and ENC-0195, cited by name.

Obligation: Cited by name, not re-run. The level statement is a typing remark and not a theorem; the Tarski clause is conditional on the arithmetic hypothesis.

### TFQ-2526 Axis 3 of the regress: relabeling blindness under a declared export

- UUID: `79333e94-370e-59a3-b515-7afdac72bfcf`
- Parent: `TFQ-0553`
- Status: `CONDITIONAL`
- DAG node: `OPS-AXIS3-RELABELING`
- Paper: [derivation](derivations/35_foc035_observer_presheaf/tfq_2526_ops_axis3_relabeling.md)

Axis 3 of WDP-CH14-T01 under three hypotheses. (i) NS-14: an injective renaming sigma of presentation tokens commutes with the transition step and with full-history replay. (ii) CL-13 (passage_charge_const): a quantity conserved by internal transitions is constant on reachable states and equals its genesis value. (iii) The verdict V reads a history only through a declared export Exp, so V = Vbar o Exp, with Exp(sigma(H)) = Exp(H) for every injective renaming sigma; this is the identical-accessible-exports premise of Proposition 3.1 of the Argon synthesis. Then V(sigma(H)) = V(H), because V(sigma(H)) = Vbar(Exp(sigma(H))) = Vbar(Exp(H)) = V(H). Without (iii) the statement is false (node OPS-REFUTED-AXIS3-WIDE). A drop in the internal defect Delta_O stays computable and renaming-invariant; whether a drop is a repair or a reinterpretation is a question about the grounding map of the tokens, which no export-reading verdict decides.

Obligation: Conditional on (iii), and on (i) and (ii) as cited, not re-run. WDP-CH14 has no node in this graph; (iii) is read as the observer-quotient reading of WDP chapter 10.

### TFQ-2531 Four defects of an earlier head of the Rust module and note

- UUID: `084d1b37-d48b-512d-a2d6-34c2d5cf50aa`
- Parent: `TFQ-2519`

At head 0a0502646 of the source repository the following were wrong. (N4) Scenario::section_count multiplied arities without a check, and the limit was compared afterwards: 64 binary singletons (2^64 assignments) wrapped to 0 in a release build, so global_support returned an empty support and is_strongly_contextual returned true. (N5) ObserverDraft::declare accepted empty and whitespace strings, and the five strings were free text copied into the receipt: a norm "L2", a terminal "always OpenObstruction" and a layer "authoritative" each yielded the l1 value, ExactRepair and authority None. (N6) Proposition A2 claimed that no claim-to-receipt function exists, carried a layer row whose second completion was not an observer, and said the refusal test dropped five components when it dropped two; and verify_noncontextual_fraction read only lp.value from the embedded solution. (N7) delta0 checked only the number of entries, delta1 and flatten1 ignored extraneous keys and pairs outside every triple, and the only delta1 delta0 = 0 test ran on the Bell nerve, which has no triple. Recomputed here: 2^64 is 0 modulo 2^64.

Obligation: Records superseded defects. The repaired behaviour is in nodes OPS-OBSERVER-DECLARATION-REFUSAL and OPS-RUST-RECEIPTS-AND-LIMITS, which are conditional (not run here).
